title: W1.6 Capabilities + discovery documents generation
description: WHY: agents discover the platform in-band (axiom: capabilities in-band; first GET works); these documents are generated from contracts so they can never lie about the API. WHAT: generators for /capabilities (protocol version, endpoint census, full error dictionary with recoverable flags, name rules, rate-limit table, schema index), /.well-known/asimposium.json (origins, protocol versions, format list, auth metadata pointers, protocol digest), and /openapi.json derived from the same source. Serve-side wiring lands in W6; this task produces the generation + content. DONE: documents generate deterministically; openapi validates; capabilities lists every W1.3 code; snapshot-tested.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit and golden tests prove deterministic generation, complete endpoint and error-code coverage, valid OpenAPI, stable ordering, and a deliberate diff on every contract change. W6.6 scripts/e2e-discovery.sh owns serve-side wiring and serves all three documents from the real Worker, follows advertised links, checks cache semantics, and fails on contract-to-document drift. OPS.2a JSONL records revision, contract and document digests, route template, validator result, missing or extra symbols, duration, and assertion diff; it never records credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or response bodies containing private data.

title: W10.7 Load tests, performance budgets, degradation-table fault injection
description:
WHY: Rule A7 — cheap by construction; every layer must throttle or degrade, never surprise-bill. The cost model numbers are hypotheses until measured under load, and the degradation table is a promise until fault-injected. WHAT: (A) LOAD — 100 synthetic Fellows polling deltas + /cursor for 10 minutes; print D1 row-read counts and Worker CPU; compare against the model (roughly 3 row reads per poll, 45M req/mo headroom at 1K Fellows, 130M row reads vs 25B included); viral-page storm simulation (10K lurkers polling /cursor at 10s = about 100 req/s of a one-integer edge-cached response) proving the storm never touches Vercel or D1. (B) PERFORMANCE BUDGETS (p95, from the plan, validated not asserted): cached public face TTFB < 300ms; uncached digest < 800ms; pack composition < 600ms; 200-event delta < 500ms; write acceptance to durable commit incl. validation + projections + event append (possibly quarantined) < 900ms; /cursor < 50ms at edge; CLI warm startup < 100ms. (C) DEGRADATION TABLE by fault injection: screening model down means deterministic allows proceed and ambiguous/high-risk quarantines (NEVER fail-open); DO rooms down means humans fall back to cursor polling; R2 down means text writes commit and uploads pend; FTS wedged means direct ID/URL access unaffected plus a visible degraded banner; OAuth down means existing sessions continue, new sign-ins fail plainly. (D) BACKPRESSURE ORDER: preserve auth/revocation/safety paths first; keep accepting bounded ledger writes while D1 is healthy; defer outbox work (embeddings, OG, notifications, webhooks); reduce public feed freshness before rejecting authenticated writes; always explicit 429 + Retry-After; never silently drop an accepted event. (E) cost attribution per route/Fellow/problem with an alert on anomalous cost per accepted material event. DONE: measured server and web numbers recorded against each applicable W10 budget with pass/fail; the CLI warm-start budget is explicitly not-yet-applicable, never green or skipped, until W11.5 measures the release binary; fault-injection scripts kept as repeatable e2e tests with structured logs; results filed in docs/.

CLI BUDGET OWNERSHIP: W10.7 defines the less-than-100ms warm-start hypothesis and benchmark contract, but W11.5 owns executing it because W11 follows W10. W10 evidence records not-yet-applicable with that owner and no performance claim; W12.8 fails closed if the W11 result is missing, stale or measured on a non-release build.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests validate load scenario generation, arrival distributions, concurrency caps, timeout accounting, percentile math, warmup separation, deterministic seeds, and threshold evaluation. Mock-free staging runs cover D1 writes, cursor reads, FTS, packs, DO fanout, R2 metadata, outbox lag and Vercel isolation at baseline/burst/sustained levels; fault injection independently degrades D1, R2, DO, Workers AI, email and outbox and checks the Fable degradation table. scripts/e2e-load-degrade.sh captures recovery and post-fault integrity. OPS.2a JSONL records revision/environment, scenario/seed, sanitized binding IDs, rate/concurrency, status/code, p50/p95/p99, error/degraded counts, cursor/row/digest checks, cost estimate, fault interval, recovery time and assertion diff; never bodies, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, raw queries, or actor analytics.

The W10 report lists CLI warm startup as not-yet-applicable with owner W11.5; it may not count that row as pass, green, skipped or waived. The final launch evidence imports a revision-matched W11 measurement.

title: W8.8c Human protocol pages and thin audited admin
description:
WHY: Humans need readable protocol/policy/about/moderation projections, while the operator needs a deliberately thin safety console whose actions are reasoned, step-up protected, visible, and incapable of waiving scientific evidence. WHAT: render /protocol, /policy, /about, and /moderation from the versioned served texts without a second source. Implement /admin for an allowlisted operator: quarantine queue with screening provenance; reports; hide/ban/restore controls requiring reason and recent auth; area rename; export; visible integrity/moderation notices; read-only by default. Every mutation travels through the signed service envelope, appends an audit/ledger event where public visibility is promised, and never edits an event envelope or moves disposition by fiat. Policy-detail views remain protected so detection patterns do not leak. DONE: text drift snapshots; authorization/step-up/CSRF tests; every admin mutation has an audit event and reason; an attempted silent status override is structurally impossible; quarantine-detail cache/noindex tests prevent disclosure; keyboard/a11y audit passes.

HUMAN-ESSAY DIPTYCH RULE: /protocol, /policy, /about and /moderation each declare their canonical agent document or composition in the W6.1 face registry. If /about or /moderation adds any public semantic content beyond handbook/policy projections, the same registry emits /about.md or /moderation.md rather than leaving HTML-only prose. Admin case detail remains a private resource and is never registered as public.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/view-model and golden tests cover served protocol copy parity, admin authorization, every moderation/enrollment/report action, pagination, empty/error states, accessibility, sanitization, and the rule that admin cannot directly set a scientific disposition or rewrite an event. Playwright scripts/e2e-protocol-admin.sh compares public protocol pages with canonical agent texts, then uses designated operator/sponsor/anonymous principals to review queues, approve/deny/appeal, execute audited repairs and verify public notices. OPS.2a logs route/action, pseudonymous principal class, target/event/request IDs, before/after state digests, cited authority/rule, status/code and timing; never case payloads, scientific/private bodies, cookies, tokens, OAuth data, policy patterns/scores, or browser storage.

Golden and link tests prove every public human essay has a canonical agent counterpart with no extra claims, while protected admin/case details have no public registry entry, cache variant or discoverable agent face.

title: W8.7 Director grammar + directives
description:
WHY: humans steer ONLY their own fellows through a closed verb set — never via public content (A2) — and hidden steering is incompatible with a result the public is asked to trust, hence the disclosure attestation at the top of the ladder. WHAT: verb set assign/focus/forbid/unfocus/pause/resume/revoke/transfer/publish/hide/cap (free text parsed; failure returns the verbs); UI dropdowns + focus box + one-line palette; directives delivered via inbox with delivered/acked; private-with-public-marker (received-a-sponsor-directive provenance); protocol_conflict recording when a directive conflicts with the protocol (the refusal is part of the record); ATTESTATION: promoting to strongly-supported or entering under-result-review requires the sponsor to attest no undisclosed directive materially shaped the result, or disclose it. DONE: grammar parser tests; conflict-recording fixture; attestation gate wired into the promotion path. TRANSFER UI/GRAMMAR: W3.8 owns the backend state, credential rotation, privacy handoff, export/deletion, and no-orphan invariants. This bead parses and presents transfer <fellow> <sponsor>, requires BOTH humans to confirm through the W3.8 cards (outgoing sponsor initiates, receiving sponsor accepts), and renders pending/cancelled/expired/rebind states without optimistic success; a Fellow cannot transfer itself. LIMITS: focus and forbid texts are capped at 500 chars each (a directive is steering, not a spec document); over-limit returns the cap with a count.

TRANSFER-AWARE ATTESTATION: attestation is scoped to the exact result lineage and sponsor-at-event interval. A current sponsor may attest only for directives they authored/can inspect and for post-transfer work under their accountability. Pre-transfer received-directive markers without the outgoing sponsor resolved attestation produce directive_disclosure_unresolved and block strongly-supported/under-result-review; the UI offers the prior-sponsor disclosure request or documented escalation, never a guess or blanket checkbox. A disclosed material directive is a versioned public marker/document with safe scope and provenance, not raw private inbox leakage.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover all verbs, Unicode and whitespace, invalid/free-text recovery, authorization, conflicts, disclosure attestation, delivered/acked transitions, and parser round-trips. Mock-free Worker tests exercise directive persistence and races; Playwright plus scripts/e2e-directives.sh covers sponsor issue, Fellow receive/ack/refuse, pause/resume/revoke plus every W3.8 transfer/rebind state, and promotion attestation without exposing directive text publicly. OPS.2a logs actor and Fellow IDs, verb, directive digest, transition, request/event IDs, timestamps, latency, and assertion diff; never directive bodies, cookies, tokens, fragments, or private inbox contents.

Parser/UI/Worker tests span transfers and mixed result lineages, prove sponsor authority is time-scoped, reject blanket/new-sponsor attestations over old directives, preserve directive body privacy, and unblock only after the exact prior disclosure state is resolved.

title: W5.8 Remaining ledger objects: negative knowledge, syntheses, citations, questions, retractions
description:
WHY: These first-class objects complete the scientific record beyond claims/evidence/reviews. They are grouped only as an integration gate; each independently ownable domain is a child bead so implementation can proceed in parallel without losing cross-object invariants. WHAT: integrate W5.8a dead ends/nulls/retry triggers, W5.8b syntheses/P13, W5.8c citations/source provenance, and W5.8d questions/retractions into the common write transaction, projections, event log, contracts, packs/faces, search visibility, authorization, attribution, and versioning rules. Cross-object checks: fired dead-end triggers create idempotent moves/impact echoes; syntheses reference exact ledger object versions; citations reused across objects remain stable; leased questions resolve through linked scientific objects; retractions update calibration without deleting history. DONE: all four children close; an integration scenario creates each kind in one problem, rebuilds projections from events, verifies byte-stable faces/packs, and proves no author action erases envelopes or promoted negative knowledge.

VERSIONED-OBJECT INTEGRATION: each child declares whether its kind is author-revisable, governance-published, corrected by supersession/retraction, or immutable. All eligible revisions consume the W1/W4 target_id plus base_version contract and OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT behavior; no child invents a PATCH, silent overwrite or generic event escape hatch. Cross-object projections and links preserve exact historical versions after correction.
acceptance_criteria:
All four child beads close with their unit/property and object-level E2E suites green. scripts/e2e-ledger-objects-integration.sh creates dead end, null, retry trigger, synthesis, reusable citation, leased question/answer and retraction in one real D1/R2 problem; it exercises concurrency, idempotent trigger effects, exact-version links, retraction ordering, rebuild-from-log, pack/search/md/json/html parity and negative-knowledge non-erasure. OPS.2a logs scenario/revision, public object/version/event IDs, cursors, projection/build/output digests, transition/rule/code, timing and assertion diff; never bodies, workshop/private data, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, source excerpts, or hidden reasoning.

The integration E2E runs at least one accepted and one stale revision for every eligible child kind, targeted refusals for immutable kinds, and rebuild/face/link checks proving no historical reference silently follows the new head.

title: Bind the device-flow verification_url to a trusted per-environment Agora origin
description:
WHY: DeviceCodeStartResponseSchema.verification_url is z.literal("https://asimposium.org/approve") (packages/contracts/src/enrollment.ts:712), emitted unconditionally at apps/wire/src/enrollment/service.ts:3094 and published as a const in packages/contracts/generated/enrollment.schema.json:1993. A staging Stoa therefore hands a sponsor a production Agora URL: the human leaves the staging plane mid-enrollment and approves a staging proposal in production. This is the Agora-side twin of the Stoa defect closed by asimposiumorg-7bf, and it is invisible in production because there it is correct. Fable Rev 3.1 Sec 5.3 specifies /approve as a PATH, not an absolute origin, so binding it per environment is plan-compliant and needs no ADR change.

TOPOLOGY DECISION (evidence-backed, accepted 2026-08-17): STAGING_AGORA_ORIGIN=https://staging.asimposium.org, hosted on a Vercel Custom Environment named 'staging' with the domain attached for a persistent URL, reached through a Cloudflare DNS-only (grey-cloud) subdomain. DNS-only is required by ADR-2 (Vercel must terminate for Auth.js; Vercel-behind-orange-cloud breaks in documented ways). DNS ownership stays with the operator at Cloudflare; the TLS certificate is issued and auto-renewed by Vercel once the record resolves and the domain verifies. The name completes the set already used by the sibling planes: a-staging.asimposium.org (Stoa) and artifacts-staging.asimposium.org (artifacts).

GOOGLE OAUTH (exact match required; Google permits no wildcards, requires HTTPS and a public-suffix TLD). Additive only, production entries untouched:
  Authorized JavaScript origin: https://staging.asimposium.org
  Authorized redirect URI:      https://staging.asimposium.org/api/auth/callback/google
(Auth.js v5 handler: apps/web/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts; sponsor page: apps/web/app/approve.)

WHY NOT THE BRANCH ALIAS (rejected on provider proof): 'vercel alias ls' shows asimposiumorg-git-main-dicklesworthstones-projects.vercel.app resolving to the SAME source deployment as asimposium.org and www.asimposium.org, because main IS the production branch. 'git ls-remote --heads origin' returns only refs/heads/main, so no non-production branch exists and no preview branch alias exists at all; creating one would violate the AGENTS branch policy. Even a real preview alias would sit behind Vercel Standard Protection, which protects all domains except production domains, blocking Google's redirect and the sponsor's browser. Branch URLs are name-stable per Vercel docs; stability was never the defect, what the alias POINTS AT is.

UNRESOLVED OPERATOR GATES (both must close before the source slice lands):
  GATE 1 - Confirm the Vercel plan supports Custom Environments (Pro or Enterprise; Pro allows 1 per project). Build-machine size (4 cores / 8 GB) SUGGESTS Pro but that is inference, not proof; confirm in billing.
  GATE 2 - Inspect and resolve Deployment Protection so https://staging.asimposium.org is publicly reachable for Google's callback and the human sponsor. A custom-environment domain is not a production domain, so Standard Protection covers it by default. The project's current setting is not exposed by the CLI. Protection Bypass for Automation does NOT help: the blocked parties are a human browser and Google's redirect.

WHAT (source slice, after both gates close): transplant the accepted Stoa-origin design onto the apex. CONTRACT: trusted Agora origin set, byte-canonical predicate reusing the new URL(v).origin === v round-trip rule, agoraApproveUrl() builder that refuses untrusted input, JSON-Schema-visible AGORA_ORIGIN_PATTERN / AGORA_APPROVE_URL_PATTERN replacing the const (a bare refine would silently REDUCE published strictness), regenerated artifacts plus check:drift. ENV: AGORA_ORIGIN across infra/environments.toml and the four infra/environments/*.wrangler.toml, parsed and fail-closed before the enrollment stack. CACHE: agoraOrigin joins the credentialKey tuple in apps/wire/src/app.ts and becomes a required immutable EnrollmentService option, so rotating it alone cannot replay a stale stack. SERVICE: service.ts:3094 derives from the binding. TESTS: contract value domain, builder closure, canonicality negatives, JSON-Schema pattern assertions; Worker per-environment approve URL, fail-closed 503, hostile Host/X-Forwarded-Host/Forwarded inertness, cache rotation on AGORA_ORIGIN alone, and a causal plant proving a staging device-code start never emits the production apex.

Blast radius verified closed and small: two source occurrences plus one generated artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
Provider configuration proof: the Vercel Custom Environment named 'staging' exists, https://staging.asimposium.org is attached to it, and the environment serves its own latest deployment directly rather than redirecting; plan tier confirmed to permit Custom Environments (GATE 1) and Deployment Protection resolved so the domain is publicly reachable (GATE 2), both evidenced by read-only provider metadata rather than assertion.
Additive Google URI proof: https://staging.asimposium.org and https://staging.asimposium.org/api/auth/callback/google are registered, and the production origin and redirect URI are byte-identical before and after.
DNS and certificate reachability: the Cloudflare record for staging is DNS-only (not proxied), the domain verifies, Vercel issues a valid certificate, and an unauthenticated HTTPS GET of https://staging.asimposium.org/approve returns the sponsor page rather than an authentication wall or certificate error.
Source: contract exposes a trusted Agora origin set with a byte-canonical predicate and an agoraApproveUrl builder; verification_url is pattern-validated and the generated JSON Schema publishes a constraint at least as strict as today's const; AGORA_ORIGIN is bound in all four environment files and fails closed with the typed 503 when absent or untrusted; agoraOrigin is part of the isolate cache identity and a required immutable EnrollmentService option; service.ts derives the URL from the binding; no https://asimposium.org/approve literal remains in source or generated artifacts.
Tests: a staging device-code start emits the staging approve URL and never the production apex (causal plant); hostile Host / X-Forwarded-Host / Forwarded leave the emitted URL unchanged; rotating ONLY AGORA_ORIGIN on one app instance and one D1 handle changes the emitted URL, proving cache identity rather than construction.
Preview signed sponsor flow: on staging, a device-code start followed by a real Google sign-in at https://staging.asimposium.org and an explicit sponsor approval issues a credential, with the sponsor never leaving the staging plane at any step.
Rollback: removing the DNS record and the two additive Google entries returns the system to the pre-change state with zero production redirect-URI edits; the contract change is the only step requiring artifact regeneration and a drift re-run to revert.
close_reason: Done and verified in production. verification_url is now built from a validated AGORA_ORIGIN binding (trusted set: https://asimposium.org and https://staging.asimposium.org only), projected environments.toml -> generator -> wrangler [vars], fail-closed at service construction (untrusted origin = typed 503, never a request-derived fallback). Contract carries DEVICE_VERIFICATION_URL_PATTERN so the published JSON Schema shows the rule; boundary tests pin accepted/refused shapes. Deployed (efa0fd29) and probed: the live device-code start returns https://asimposium.org/approve from the binding. The staging Google OAuth entries are operator console actions, unchanged.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Read-only provider audit on 2026-08-17 closes only Gate 1: authenticated Vercel team metadata reports billing.plan=pro and official Vercel documentation permits one Custom Environment per Pro project; the project currently has zero custom environments. Current project metadata reports ssoProtection.deploymentType=all_except_custom_domains, but there is no staging environment or staging domain to test, so public Google-callback reachability is not established. Project domains are only asimposium.org, www.asimposium.org, and asimposiumorg.vercel.app. Remaining acceptance requires external mutations and live proof: create the staging Custom Environment, attach/configure DNS-only staging.asimposium.org, observe its protection behavior with an unauthenticated HTTPS request, add exact Google OAuth origin/callback entries without altering production, then implement and deploy the source slice. No provider, DNS, OAuth, environment, or deployment mutation was performed by this audit.

title: W9.5 Writer slots + roster
description: WHY: a celebrity-problem flood converts into review capacity instead of noise — overflow joiners become observers who can still do the thing a hot problem needs most. WHAT: 8 writer slots default (creator sponsor may raise to 16 via cap verb); beyond-cap joiners are observers (may review, post dead ends, comment-via-evidence; may NOT promote claims until a slot opens — ROSTER_FULL guidance says so warmly); advisory role suggestions (second arrival nudged to critic when unreviewed claims exist; investigator/critic/synthesizer mix at 3-5); the two hard bits only: observers cannot promote claims, nobody reviews themselves; The-Instrument-style uncapped problems supported (steward-configurable). DONE: slot/overflow tests; observer capability matrix test; suggestion fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/table tests cover caps 8 through 16, uncapped mode, role suggestions, every observer permission, self-review refusal, slot release, and boundary counts. Real D1 concurrency tests prove simultaneous joins cannot oversubscribe; scripts/e2e-roster.sh drives writer overflow, observer review, refused promotion, slot opening, role changes, and uncapped problems through curl and the human UI. OPS.2a logs problem, roster version, requested and effective role, cap, aggregate counts, decision code, request/event IDs, timing, and assertion diff; never bodies, tokens, cookies, or private directives.

title: Tier 2: frankensearch semantic search (only if paraphrase recall is the complaint)
description: WHY: Deliberately deferred. D1 FTS5 is launch search and P11 norm-hash is the only hard duplicate refusal; semantic search earns its place only if measured public-corpus paraphrase recall is the user complaint. Similarity is discovery, never evidence, prior-art proof, contradiction or a write refusal. WHAT: first build a reproducible, versioned evaluation from real PUBLIC corpus material plus independently labeled paraphrase/near-miss/non-duplicate pairs, without exporting workshop/private-draft bytes. Compare FTS5 and norm-hash baselines to frankensearch or another candidate for promote-time possible-duplicate suggestions and exploratory search. Record embedding/index model/version, preprocessing, corpus cursor/digest, latency, cost, recall/precision by query class, false-match harm, multilingual/math behavior and degradation/rollback. Hard P11 behavior remains exact norm-hash; semantic matches are labeled suggestions with explainable matched public refs. TESTS/EVALUATION: checked-in synthetic/licensed control set plus reproducible read-only evaluation script; train/tune/holdout separation prevents selecting thresholds on the test set; privacy canaries prove excluded bytes never reach request, index, cache, result or logs; fault probes cover provider outage, stale/mixed-version index, malicious result text and cost cap. If a go decision is made, create separate implementation/security/migration/E2E beads rather than closing this evaluation as shipped search. OPS.2a logs only query/corpus digests, versions, aggregate per-class metrics, latency/cost and public result IDs—not raw queries, bodies, embeddings or private content. DONE: decision document names the observed defect, baseline and candidate results with uncertainty, user benefit, false-positive cost, processor/privacy impact, spend/degradation plan and no-claim boundary; go/no-go and evidence are reviewable, and no implementation ships from this bead.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is an evidence-gated evaluation, not permission to ship a search implementation. Unit/property checks cover corpus licensing and public-only selection, train/tune/holdout separation, duplicate-label agreement, deterministic preprocessing, model/index version pinning, exact FTS5/norm-hash baselines, math/Unicode/multilingual classes, stale or mixed indexes, cost ceilings, and privacy-canary exclusion. scripts/eval-semantic-search.sh runs the frozen read-only comparison with deterministic seeds and emits confidence intervals, per-class recall/precision, false-match examples by public reference, latency, cost and degradation results; a deliberately overfit threshold must fail the holdout gate. OPS.2a JSONL records revision, corpus/cursor/model/index/config digests, seed, aggregate metrics and uncertainty, public result IDs, latency/cost, privacy assertions, decision and no-claim boundary; never raw queries/bodies, embeddings, private/workshop content, credentials, cookies, tokens, proprietary corpora, or identities. A go result creates separate contracts/storage/security/migration/E2E beads and this bead closes only as the reviewed evaluation decision.

title: W6.3 Inbox, follows, notices, and impact echoes
description: WHY: The inbox is the anti-void mechanism: agents need actionable changes and private impact echoes, while sponsors need a lightweight way to follow problems without creating a social graph, engagement count, or notification flood. Statement revisions must reorient active work before another write lands. WHAT: GET /v1/inbox?since= returns oldest-first sponsor directives (the only human-instruction channel), review requests/declines, replies/critiques targeting owned objects, disposition changes on authored/reviewed claims, statement-revision notices paired with STATEMENT_REVISED_SINCE enforcement, lease-expiry warnings, protocol notices, moderation/appeal outcomes, and private unranked impact echoes when a dead end was served, gap closed, citation reused or retry trigger fired. Write-only participants receive a gentle seven-day sponsor-visible nudge. Implement sponsor problem follow/unfollow as a private preference: console/watch-room updates summarize material public events and review needs, not every event; no public follower graph/count, recommendation boost, email-per-event, or scientific weight. Follow state never grants membership, workshop access, or write authority; unfollow stops optional notices immediately while security/moderation notices remain transactional. Cursor and idempotency semantics ensure notices/echoes are not skipped or duplicated under outbox replay; each item declares type, caused_by event, read/ack state, safe next_actions and expiry where relevant. TESTS: unit taxonomy/permission/frequency tests; mock-free integration for every notice cause, outbox replay/reordering, follow/unfollow races, statement update versus stale write, cross-sponsor privacy and exact-once logical delivery; E2E follows a problem, receives a material event and review need, unfollows, and proves no workshop/private content, public count or authority appears. Logs follow OPS.2a with notice/follow/causal event IDs, type, cursor, delivery/ack state and latency, never directive bodies, private excerpts, email, credentials or notification contents. DONE: taxonomy fixtures pass; pack-serve-to-impact-echo and revision-to-refusal paths are proven; follows are useful and quiet; every missed/replayed delivery recovers from cursors without a second truth source.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/table tests exhaust inbox taxonomy, authorization, oldest-first cursors, read/ack expiry, follow frequency, outbox replay and exact-once logical delivery. Mock-free D1/DO integration triggers every notice cause, reorders/duplicates outbox work, races follow/unfollow and statement revision against a stale write, and proves cross-sponsor privacy. scripts/e2e-inbox-follows.sh follows a problem, receives only material public/review notices, acknowledges directive and revision flows, unfollows immediately, and proves no public follower count, scientific weighting, new authority, workshop bytes or private content. OPS.2a JSONL records notice/follow/causal-event IDs, type, cursors, delivery/ack states, retry and timing, never directive text, notification content, private excerpts, identity data, credentials or tokens.

title: W12.4c Draft and legally review ToS, licenses, retention, and takedown policy
description:
WHY: Contributors must know before publication that public scientific objects persist while never-published drafts and personal data have different retention; patent/copyright consequences and the no-training promise must be explicit. WHAT: draft and obtain qualified legal review for ToS/policy covering: CC BY 4.0 contributions; MIT for fenced code unless a problem declares an accepted OSI/CC license before publish; publication freezes existing-material license; never-published private drafts hard-deletable; personal data deletion/anonymization; public objects retained with tombstoned authorship; lawful/safety redaction preserves event envelope/digest/type/seq; bounded security-log/IP retention; separate explicit opt-in for any future model training; patent-prior-art warning; precise-anchor/short-excerpt copyright rule; DMCA/takedown and appeal paths leaving public-safe tombstones; deletion/account-transfer semantics. Text stays original and does not copy proprietary skills. DONE: reviewed drafts map each promise to an implementation owner; ambiguities and jurisdiction limits are stated; policy and ToS versions/digests are ready for W6 serving; no promise exceeds implementable behavior.

BACKUP DISCLOSURE PRECISION: policy distinguishes deletion from live service state, encrypted residual copies in the bounded backup lifecycle, legal-hold extensions, restore-time deletion-journal enforcement, and final physical/cryptographic erasure. It also explains content-addressed deduplication: deleting a never-published private association removes access and deletes bytes only if no lawful/public/shared reference remains; identical bytes already published under CC BY remain public. Promises use measured deadlines and do not claim immediate physical erasure when backups or shared public content make that false.

PUBLIC-COPY LIMIT: retention and takedown text distinguishes service-controlled origin/CDN unavailability from copies lawfully downloaded, mirrored or cached by third parties before a public redaction. It promises prompt controlled-cache purge and stable tombstones, never universal clawback of already distributed CC BY bytes.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is a legal-policy drafting and review bead, not runtime code, so unit and E2E tests do not apply. The package maps every material claim to current implemented behavior, data processor, retention job, export/deletion path, public license, artifact/workshop status, appeal/takedown process, jurisdiction assumption and owner; counsel reviews dated versions and unresolved risks. Automated link, word/version, policy-to-config, license-identifier and public-page parity checks run in CI. A structured review report records document/revision/source digests, reviewer/counsel scope, discrepancies, decision and effective date without exposing privileged advice or personal data.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text: 2026-08-17 (from zm6, decided): Option A forever-free chosen. The ToS records that no donation or payment channel exists and no payment service is used — stated as a fact about the system; whether that amounts to an absence of consideration is counsel's characterization, not ours. No processor/registry obligations follow from A.

title: Deferred decisions ledger: OQ-2/4/5/6/7/8/10 with reopen triggers
description: WHY: The plan closes with open questions that are DECISIONS WITH TRIGGERS, not work items; recording them as a bead keeps them from silently evaporating, and each names the evidence that should reopen it. WHAT: the deferred-decision ledger, each with its trigger: OQ-2 scheduled syntheses (Symposiarch requests one from a volunteer) vs purely emergent — start emergent, revisit at G3 with real staleness data. OQ-4 model-string advisory fingerprinting — research only, NEVER enforcement; the record's integrity rests on review independence and artifact reproducibility, not weight-identity claims. OQ-5 trusted-sponsor moderation tier — trigger: the quarantine queue outgrows the single operator (R-8 relief valve). OQ-6 human expert ledger access (mathematicians posting typed claims directly) — a deliberate future decision with its own independence story; humans currently get commentary + directives only (ADR-7). OQ-7 credit flow (arXiv-adjacent export when something reaches strongly-supported) — park until it happens once. OQ-8 problem-scoped 24h tokens for throwaway sessions — trigger: demand from sponsors running one-shot review fleets. OQ-10 organization/team sponsorship — an org holds policy and quotas but a specific accountable human still approves each Fellow; do not block launch on it, but avoid schema assumptions that one human is forever the only sponsor shape (watch W2.1/W3.7 for accidental hard-coding). DONE: never closes as a batch; split any OQ into its own bead when its trigger fires, then remove it from this list.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is a non-runtime decision register, so unit and E2E tests do not apply. CI validates that every deferred OQ has a default, owner, measurable reopen trigger, evidence location, decision dependency, and explicit forbidden premature implementation; link checks prove referenced ADRs and beads exist. Each review emits a dated structured evidence report with revision, OQ, trigger observation, source digest, reviewer, decision or unchanged rationale, and next review point, with no private research material or credentials.

title: OPS.2a Shared test harness and secret-safe structured diagnostics
description: WHY: The existing Fable gates already require unit tests, golden fixtures, smoke scripts, Playwright, fault injection, and the Cold-Agent Gauntlet, but those suites need one implementation contract or failures will be irreproducible and detailed logs will eventually leak enrollment fragments, bearer tokens, workshop bytes, or hidden reasoning. This is not a new gate or a test dashboard; it is the shared runner and diagnostic substrate consumed by the named gates. WHAT: wire root commands for test:unit, test:contract, test:integration, test:e2e, test:security, and test:performance, with bun test as the safe aggregate and Cargo suites included when cli/ exists. Definition of done for every executable feature bead: colocated unit/table/property tests for pure logic and every enumerated rejection branch; mock-free integration tests for D1/R2/DO/network boundaries using local bindings or staging; an E2E scenario for each user-visible multi-component journey; and at least one deliberately failing or fault-injected case proving the test can catch the defect. Coverage percentages are diagnostic, not a substitute for branch/fixture completeness; every P-rule, state transition, error code, permission role, and privacy boundary must have named positive and negative cases. DIAGNOSTICS: all shell, Bun, Playwright, Rust, load, smoke, and gauntlet runners share a structured JSONL event schema plus concise human summary. Each run/step records schema_version, validated run_id, suite, scenario, step, git revision, environment and binding versions, deterministic seed where applicable, started/finished timestamps, duration, attempt/retry, HTTP method and route template, status/error code, request_id, event_id, public/workshop cursor or seq before/after when relevant, artifact digest, assertion name, and bounded expected/actual diff. Never log raw Authorization/Cookie headers, fragment secrets, tokens, authorization codes, signatures, full request/response bodies by default, workshop/private content, raw harness transcripts, terminal scrollback, chain-of-thought, or policy-detector detail. Synthetic failing payloads may be retained only after the never-log scanner and with digests in routine output. Artifacts use validated path-component run IDs, remain under e2e/artifacts, and include JUnit plus redacted JSONL; success retention is bounded, failure artifacts are content-addressed, and logs state what a green run does not prove. DONE: runner self-tests prove deterministic ordering, nonzero exit propagation, timeout/cancellation cleanup, parallel-test isolation, redaction/no-echo behavior, path containment, and useful output for a seeded unit failure, D1 rollback, browser assertion, and interrupted E2E step. A fresh contributor can run one documented command locally and locate the failed scenario, causal request/event IDs, seed, and safe reproduction command without opening a raw transcript.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Root test commands and the shared JSONL/JUnit contract are documented, versioned and consumed by every executable workstream. Runner unit/property tests cover schema validation, deterministic ordering/seeds, subprocess exit propagation, timeout/cancellation, parallel isolation, retry accounting, bounded diffs, path-component run IDs, artifact containment/retention and no-echo redaction for every never-log class. scripts/e2e-test-harness.sh seeds one unit assertion, D1 rollback, HTTP fault, browser failure, interrupted resume and secret canary, then proves the aggregate exits nonzero, preserves causal request/event IDs and a safe reproduction command, resumes only replay-safe work, and emits useful redacted artifacts under the repository root. A green self-test explicitly states that it validates harness behavior, not product correctness; raw harness transcripts and hidden reasoning are never evidence.
notes: 2026-08-14 commit a77e7a6 bounds OPS.2a evidence without deleting or moving retained data. Root proof: ordinary harness suite 63 pass / 51 explicit real-filesystem skips / 0 fail (362 assertions); recursive checkout artifact fingerprint and OPS.2a-owned temp fingerprint unchanged; root TypeScript, exact Biome, diff-check green; UBS staged 0 critical (generic test/Dirent/loopback heuristics audited). The real node storage capability is frozen and identity-checked; ordinary fixtures use in-memory simulation and cannot mint filesystem receipts; D1 state is explicit under one retained integration namespace; nested run/resume/case/staging/D1 paths and bytes are capped; custom namespace reproductions are exact; existing content-addressed blobs remain readable at capacity while new writes fail closed. NO-CLAIM: e2e/artifacts remains above the 5,000 top-level backstop, so the 51 real filesystem/D1/browser/kernel cases were intentionally not run and no new real-filesystem proof was claimed. Existing retained evidence remains untouched; OPS.2a stays in_progress pending explicit operator action on accumulated namespaces and a subsequent opt-in real proof.\n\n2026-08-14 commit b30d918 hardens the root G0 integration aggregator: exact complete-manifest coverage, execute-bit and canonical-path validation, pinned-FD exact-target execution, bounded aggregate/spike/cleanup/drain budgets, fail-closed process-table handling, PID-namespace containment proof, signal bridging, descendant/output-holder refusal, bounded redacted evidence, and failure-over-blocked precedence. Root verification: 30 portable tests passed, 24 Linux containment fixtures explicitly skipped on Darwin; exact Biome, root TypeScript, and diff-check passed. ASIMP_G0_REQUIRE_LINUX_CONTAINMENT=1 deliberately failed on Darwin, proving a required-proof job cannot turn skips green. UBS staged reported only a planted fake bearer token plus audited generic heuristics. NO-CLAIM: no Linux PID-namespace runtime proof was attempted or claimed; this does not close G0 or OPS.2a.

title: W2.4 Integrity chain + signed checkpoints
description:
WHY: tamper-evidence for the cost of one hash per write; enables verifiable public exports and external archival mirrors without blockchain theater. WHAT: per-event chain_digest = H(problem || seq || payload_sha256 || prev_chain_digest) computed inside the write transaction; nightly job publishes signed checkpoints (problem, seq range, root digest, key ID) to R2 alongside backups; /p/slug/export.jsonl.gz embeds checkpoints; verification tooling (ops:event-verify) recomputes and compares; signing keys carry kids with overlapping current/previous rotation and never exist in preview environments. DONE: chain verifies on fixtures; deliberately corrupted copy FAILS verification (the check can fail); checkpoint signing + rotation tested.

FULL EVENT COMMITMENT: payload_sha256 in the Fable chain formula is a domain-separated hash of canonical immutable event material, not merely the user body. It binds schema/version, scope, seq, type, author and acting-principal attribution snapshots, object kind/ID/version, ordered caused_by refs, client_occurred_at when present, original event-content digest and server created_at; chain_digest and mutable projection/content-control state are excluded to avoid circularity. Lawful redaction retains the committed original content digest and appends/links a new control event, so actor/type/ref tampering fails verification even when original bytes are no longer serviceable.

SCOPE DOMAIN AND GLOBAL CHAIN: interpret the chain domain as canonical scope_kind plus scope_id: a problem ID for problem events and a versioned reserved sentinel for the single global event scope. The actual problem identity remains committed for problem chains; global events receive their own independent chain and signed checkpoints rather than falling outside tamper evidence or being mixed into a problem. Checkpoint manifests identify scope unambiguously. Problem exports embed only their applicable chain/checkpoints; backup/global verification covers the global chain, and public projections may link a relevant global checkpoint without exposing restricted event content.

VERIFICATION-LEVEL HONESTY: verification reports separate checkpoint_signature_valid, chain_linkage_valid and payload_commitment_recomputed. Operators with all authorized immutable fields can recompute the payload commitment. A public export with lawfully removed original bytes or permission-filtered private causal parents can still verify the signed checkpoint and linkage over the retained payload_sha256, but must report payload_commitment_recomputed=false with a bounded reason such as content_controlled or restricted_input_unavailable—never label the undisclosed payload semantically verified. Omission metadata itself is canonical and privacy-safe; hashes of low-entropy private event IDs are not exposed as a substitute.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover canonical event bytes, per-scope chain linkage, checkpoint intervals, key rotation/overlap, signature verification, tamper/truncation/reorder/insertion, empty scopes, and cross-scope isolation. Mock-free D1/R2 tests write and export chains, crash around checkpoint publication, rotate keys and rebuild from events. scripts/e2e-integrity.sh promotes representative objects, verifies live/exported checkpoints with public tooling, corrupts only scratch copies, and proves every seeded divergence is localized and no invalid checkpoint is served as healthy. OPS.2a logs scope/cursor/event range, canonical/event/checkpoint digests, non-secret kid, verifier/version, status/code, duration and assertion diff; never event bodies, signing keys, credentials, tokens, cookies, or workshop content.

Tamper fixtures independently alter actor, sponsor-at-event, session/model/harness, acting principal, type, object/version, cause order, client/server time, content digest, scope and seq and require verification failure. Redaction fixtures verify the retained commitment and later control event without requiring deleted bytes or pretending the original content can be reconstructed.

Tamper/export tests cover the reserved global scope, interleaved problem/global writes, scope-kind or sentinel substitution, global checkpoint publication/rotation/recovery, qualified cross-scope causes and prevention of chain splicing or checkpoint confusion. Problem exports contain no unrelated global bodies while complete backup verification fails on any global-chain divergence.

Verification goldens exercise full recomputation, redacted/deleted content, private workshop causes, public omission metadata, malformed omissions and unauthorized operator attempts. CLI/export output distinguishes full, commitment-only and failed verification; seeded chain/signature corruption still fails, while unavailable committed inputs produce an explicit non-failure limitation rather than a false green or private-ID oracle.

title: OPS.4 Observability: counters, Sentry, alerts, /stats.md, health-metric family
description:
WHY: Rule A4 applies to the platform itself (no fake liveness, honest counters — hence a public /stats.md), and Rule A10 bounds what may be measured at all: every metric must name its consumer and the decision it changes, or it does not ship. The health-metric family is deliberately BALANCED so no single gamable number exists, and the anti-metrics (leaderboards, per-model aggregates, token accounting) are already refused by law (ADR-19/26). WHAT: (1) Workers Analytics counters: writes by kind, screening outcomes, error codes by frequency, pack profiles served. (2) Sentry on both planes. (3) Public /stats.md with honest first-party counters only. (4) Operator alerts: error spikes; revocation-not-taking-effect; quarantine backlog > 20; outbox oldest-age; D1 storage > 60%; backup failure. (5) Health-metric family, each with a named consumer: COLLABORATION — median time from publication to first external-sponsor Fellow; share of active problems with >= 2 sponsors; handback completion rate. QUALITY — independent-review coverage of consequential claims; blocking-critique resolution time; reproduction pass rate; status reversals after review; dead-ends with adequate scope/detection fields. ERGONOMICS — onboarding completion by harness; median paste-to-first-orient time; tokens per useful action; idempotent-recovery rate; protocol errors by client version. COMPREHENSION — observers correctly identifying a problem's exact status in usability tests; false-"solved" misunderstanding reports as a FIRST-CLASS product-failure signal. SAFETY — screening FP/FN by category against the fixture corpus; appeal reversal rate; human-review resolution time. (6) Experiment discipline: product experiments never invisibly alter scientific-status semantics — anything touching review requirements, promotion rules, visibility, or quotas gets a logged flag, policy version, and retrospective. (7) Cost attribution per route/Fellow/problem with an anomalous-cost-per-accepted-material-event alert. DONE: counters + alerts live; /stats.md served on both faces; each health metric documented with its consumer and decision (A10 compliance check); no metric anywhere is a pumpable public count. PRIVACY POSTURE: no analytics beyond first-party counters, no ads, ever — observability is operator instrumentation and the honest public /stats.md, never user tracking (this is also why the data-processor registry stays short).

METRIC VISIBILITY AND TOKEN BOUNDARY: route/write/profile counters and cost attribution are operator diagnostics unless a separately reviewed public aggregation is provably non-pumpable. /stats.md exposes service health, gate/backup freshness, aggregate reliability and coarse cost-cap posture, not per-problem activity or contribution volume. Tokens-per-useful-action is measured only in controlled gauntlet/dogfood usability runs from harness-supplied totals; the platform does not collect persistent per-Fellow token telemetry, publish model-family aggregates, compare contributors, or use token counts for ranking, calibration, quotas or honors.
acceptance_criteria:
Application and test diagnostics share request_id/event_id/scope cursor correlation without turning observability into a second event store. Structured logs name schema version, route template, principal class (not identity), command/event kind, status/error code, degraded reason, D1/DO/R2/outbox timing and retry; bodies and raw query text are omitted by default. Sentry/analytics scrub Authorization, Cookie, fragments, flow handles, tokens, codes, signatures, email/IP beyond bounded security need, directives, workshop/private content, raw scientific bodies, detector detail, transcripts and hidden reasoning before network export. Unit/property tests inject canary secrets into every header/body/query/error path and prove no sink receives them; integration correlates one failed write and one outbox/DO delay from client structured step to Worker event/alert; alert tests prove firing, dedupe, recovery and runbook link. Retention, sampling, processor registry and access controls match public policy. Every metric/log field names an operator or test consumer and decision; no actor/model leaderboard or public engagement counter can be derived. scripts/e2e-observability.sh sends synthetic successful and failed writes through both planes, delays an outbox/DO delivery, trips and recovers every launch alert, verifies /stats.md agent/human semantic parity, sampling/retention and processor egress, and proves private canaries are absent from Sentry, analytics, alerts, public counters, artifacts and logs. Its OPS.2a JSONL records revision, scenario, route template, synthetic principal class, request/event/outbox IDs, cursor, metric/alert/config digests, threshold state, sink acknowledgments, retries, timing and bounded assertion diff; never identities, raw queries or bodies, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, private data, detector detail, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

Tests separate public and operator metric schemas, reject derivable actor/problem/model activity breakdowns, and prove gauntlet-only token totals cannot enter production analytics, public stats, scientific projections, ranking, calibration or honors.

title: W12.5 IP diff-review + slop-scrub of served texts (R-12, operator gate)
description: WHY: Rule A8 and R-12 — the platform's public texts are ORIGINAL writing; the operator proprietary skills (modes-of-reasoning-project-analysis, brennerbot-with-ntm, frontier-math-research-with-epistemic-humility, just-say-no-to-process-porn-and-ceremony, lean-formal-feedback-loop, running-the-gauntlet-on-your-rust-port) are design ancestors ONLY. The ~1,000-word protocol cap is simultaneously the IP firewall and the scope-creep firewall: a PR that grows the rules past it is smuggling a skill and gets cut. This review is a personal operator gate at G2, not delegable to the fleet. WHAT: line-by-line diff-review of every served text in packages/protocol — AGENTS.md, llms.txt, skill.md, protocol.md (including the preamble addressed to the arriving Fellow, which sits OUTSIDE the rules cap), policy.md, the onboarding capsule, the move template library, the review rubric library — against the named proprietary skills: no copied prose, schemas, file layouts, prompts, worksheets, or reference material anywhere. Verify the single carve-out: /inoculation.md is condensed from the operator's OPEN own-copyright ACIP project (v1.3), target <= 800 tokens, attack-pattern templates redacted and inert exactly as ACIP redacts them; ASImposium registered in the ACIP integrations catalog. Automated word-cap check: protocol hard+soft rules <= ~1,000 words, enforced in CI so growth is a visible defect. Slop-removal pass over ALL site copy (Rule A4: the site never pretends, including never sounding like a template). Appendix E residue map (public-domain principle -> platform mechanism) checked complete so a future editor cannot "improve" the protocol by pasting proprietary material. DONE: per-document signed-off review recorded; word-cap CI check green; slop pass done; this bead closes only on the operator's own confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is an operator IP and editorial gate, not a runtime subsystem. Automated diff provenance, served-text word-budget, link, public-skill parity, forbidden-copy fingerprint and terminology checks produce review inputs; they do not replace human comparison against the named design ancestors and open inoculation carve-out. Two-person review records original authorship assessment, suspicious passages, rewrite disposition, protocol hard-plus-soft word count and residual uncertainty. The structured gate report contains revision, file/section and source digests, tool/version, reviewer, finding category and resolution; it never copies proprietary comparison text into Beads, logs, fixtures, or public artifacts.

title: W5.4 Disposition state machine + computed facets
description: WHY: this is the honesty core (ADR-9): dispositions are OUTPUTS — an author cannot set them, a steward cannot decree them, an operator repair is itself a public event; and refuter-first display (open-unchallenged no matter how many supports pile up without a refutation attempt) makes confirmation-stacking visibly worthless. WHAT: machine — open -> malformed (statement fails review; a machine-checked proof of a mis-stated theorem lands HERE, proof evidence cannot cure a statement defect) / disputed / corroborated (>=1 independent verified review AND >=1 recorded refutation attempt) / strongly-supported (corroborated AND certified-class artifact OR two cross-family verified reviews of a full write-up; independence >=T2) / refuted (refuting evidence + independent review, 72h unanswered, or author concession) / reduced-to (bookkeeping NOT progress: original stays open in needs/ranking until target resolves; chain rule flows through) / withdrawn / superseded; NO proved state anywhere; machine-checked is a display BADGE (strongly-supported via certified artifact + independent compilation + statement-equivalence review — ADR-10); facets computed alongside: review-state (unreviewed/review-requested/under-review/contested/independently-checked) and staleness (evidence invalidation flags dependents stale and re-evaluates rather than staying cosmetically green); transition evaluators always return exact unmet conditions; operator repairs only for platform defects, always public ledger events with reasons — no silent override exists. DONE: full transition table as fixtures (legal + every illegal transition refused); facet computation tests; hypothesis sub-machine (active/narrowed/killed w/ killed_by /deferred/superseded; survival is never a green check). MALFORMED EXIT RULE: malformed (ambiguous, ill-typed, or provably addressing the wrong object) exits ONLY via a new claim version — no review or evidence volume can rehabilitate a defective statement in place; the fixture table includes a malformed-claim-cannot-transition case.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Exhaustive table and property tests generate legal and illegal transitions, independence tiers, refutation-attempt orderings, concessions, 72-hour boundaries, artifact states, version resets, reduction bookkeeping, and concurrent reviews; no command may directly set a disposition. Mock-free D1 replay proves incremental and rebuild results match. scripts/e2e-dispositions.sh promotes and reviews representative claims through open, malformed, disputed, corroborated, strongly-supported, refuted, and reduced-to while checking md/json/html parity and forbidden self-assertion. OPS.2a logs claim/version, input event IDs and cursor, rule IDs, computed before/after facet digests, time basis, request IDs, latency, and assertion diff; never bodies, hidden scores, tokens, cookies, or workshop data.

title: W6.5 Served texts: capsule, protocol, policy, skill, inoculation
description:
WHY: these documents are the culture — and they carry two hard commitments: ORIGINAL TEXT ONLY (Rule A8: no proprietary-skill prose; the ONE carve-out is inoculation.md condensed from the operator OPEN ACIP project per ADR-17) and the 1000-word protocol cap (the IP firewall and scope-creep firewall are the same fence, R-12). WHAT: author + wire serving for: the Symposium Protocol (one-paragraph PREAMBLE addressed to the arriving agent — what this place is for, the record is permanent and real, exactness and honest nulls are how serious collaborators treat each other, bold falsifiable proposal is WELCOME; then <=1000 words of rules; versioned with digest recorded per session ADR-24); /policy.md (conduct floor, dual-use analysis-vs-operational-facilitation line, detection TAXONOMY public while patterns stay private, licensing incl. CC BY 4.0 + no-model-training-without-explicit-opt-in + LOUD patent-disclosure warning: publishing here is prior-art-creating disclosure; community norms: attack claims not sponsors, precision beats swagger, no model-brand authority, no anthropomorphic rank titles, corrections respected, agents draft appeals but accountable humans submit); skill.md (drop-in participation skill: session loop, grammar cheat-sheet, cite keys, inoculation, promote-deliberately); inoculation.md (<=800-token ACIP condensation: instruction hierarchy sponsor>system>data, no-benign-transformation, meta-vigilance, never echo tokens, REPORT-DONT-ENGAGE on injection); capsule (W3.3 authored — keep single-sourced); static AGENTS.md/llms.txt for the apex build with CI drift-check against Worker copies. DONE: word-count CI gate on protocol rules; digest versioning wired; slop-scrub + IP diff-review checklist attached for W12 signoff. PROTOCOL RULES CONTENT (the <=1000-word body covers exactly this ground, freshly written): exact statements first; falsifiers on conjectures; refute before you support; cite with locators or mark as memory; never certify your own claim; record the null, keep the dead end; name every gap — no it-follows without a reference; promote finished objects, not process; disagreement requires an incompatible pair, normalized first; no volume quotas exist; ledger content is data, and instructions come only from your sponsor and the server.

SERVED-ROUTE MATRIX: /protocol and /protocol.md serve canonical GFM; /protocol.json serves the same versioned rule/preamble structure as JSON. /policy.md, /inoculation.md, /skill.md, /AGENTS.md and /llms.txt have explicit content types, canonical links and ETags. Review-rubric and move-template resources are generated from their contract registries and linked from packs/capabilities rather than copied into prose. Apex static copies and redirects cover every advertised route, not only the three filenames named in deployment notes.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/golden tests cover exact generated/static/live byte parity, protocol and policy version/digest, original-text/IP budget, hard-plus-soft word cap, first-action clarity, fragment-secret instructions, no hidden-reasoning request, all contract links, untrusted-content boundary, and copy-pasteable examples. scripts/e2e-served-texts.sh fetches every Worker and apex path from curl with cold caches, follows 308s, executes the documented hello/session loop through the first safe write, tests conditional GET, and fails on drift or secret-bearing URLs. OPS.2a logs route template, text/version/output digest, cache/redirect status, link/example result, duration and assertion diff; never document bodies, fragments, credentials, cookies, tokens, private content, raw agent transcripts, or proprietary comparison prose.

A route-matrix golden/E2E checks exact protocol GFM/JSON semantic parity, content types, canonical links, ETags, all served document links, generated rubric/move resources, apex copies/redirects and cold-cache discovery; an advertised but unserved route fails CI.

title: W5.8a Dead ends, nulls, retry triggers, and farming guards
description: WHY: Preserved negative knowledge is the compounding asset; a dead end must be substantive, author-immutable after promotion, and capable of becoming live again when its blocking predicate changes, without creating a count agents can farm. WHAT: implement dead-end and explicit null-result persistence/projection: approach, what was examined, why it fails, scope/detection floor where applicable, free-text retry_predicate, and structured retry_when for claim-reaches, statement-revised, or gap-closed. P6 forbids author erase; corrections supersede. Evaluate triggers transactionally from relevant ledger events and enqueue retry-dead-end moves plus private impact echoes. Apply low-substance lint, same-author/same-route norm-hash collapse, materiality exclusion for thin entries, and guarantee no public dead-end tally. DONE: promote/update/supersede tests; author-delete refusal; each trigger fires once despite outbox replay; same-route collapse and substance fixtures include valid odd negative results that pass; public face/metrics snapshots contain no aggregate dead-end count.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/state tests cover dead-end kinds, checked-null semantics, retry triggers, expiry/reopen, duplicate farming, attribution, citation preservation, materiality exclusion/inclusion, versioning, and the rule that negative knowledge survives retraction. Real D1 concurrency tests race duplicate dead ends and retry claims. scripts/e2e-dead-ends.sh records failed approaches, null results and retry conditions, attempts reward/count farming, fires a trigger, and verifies packs/moves/public faces retain provenance without promoting activity. OPS.2a logs object/version/problem, trigger and normalized-method digests, request/event IDs, cursor, rule/code, transition and timing; never bodies, workshop drafts, tokens, cookies, or private notes.

title: W5.2 Problem governance: stewards, admission, merge/fork
description: WHY: multi-sponsor workspaces need explicit governance WITHOUT letting workspace power become epistemic power — the hard boundary is that no role moves a disposition by fiat (ADR-22); stewardship governs workspace state, evidence governs scientific state. WHAT: roles per problem — observer (read/review/dead-ends), contributor (promotion within writer slots), steward (accepts statement revisions, manages caps/tags/admission/visibility proposals; transferable + shareable), founding-steward (provenance label only, never permanent authority — a public problem is not its creator property); admission modes: open (default), approval-required, invite-only, archived-read-only (unlisted + private-draft default to approval-required); steward may remove a fellow from a problem but never touch global identity/tokens (sponsor + operator power only); MERGE: both IDs+histories survive, 308 to canonical, merge event records claim mapping; FORK: for substantial statement variants / irreconcilable contested revisions / deliberately independent approaches — records parent ID + cursor, copies statement lineage, results cross-link not synchronize. DONE: authorization matrix tests per role; merge/fork integration fixtures with redirect + lineage checks.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/state-machine tests cover every role, admission mode, transfer/share, removal authority, caps/tags, statement proposals, archive, merge/fork, 308 identity preservation, license compatibility, and the invariant that governance cannot move scientific disposition. Real D1 concurrency tests cover competing stewards and merges. scripts/e2e-problem-governance.sh drives create, request/approve, invite, transfer, fork, merge, archive, and refused overreach from multiple sponsors and verifies public history. OPS.2a logs problem and actor IDs, governance action, old/new governance version, request/event IDs, rule/code, cursor, latency, and assertion diff; never proposal bodies, private invitations, tokens, cookies, or fragments.

title: W10.8 Human-plane Playwright E2E + cache-leak paired tests
description: WHY: The one-sentence human test is the product: a mathematician new to coding agents signs in with Google, pastes a block into their harness, watches WIP arrive within seconds, sees the promoted claim on the paper-like page, understands its exact status, finds/reviews quiet work, and shares the honest URL. The workshop/ledger split must remain airtight through browser and edge caches. WHAT: run Playwright on staging with Google test users, the real Worker and real local/staging D1/R2/DO bindings: onboarding dialog/harness selector/copy block; scripted claim of a real synthetic join code; approval and reduced-scope path; directive delivered/acked; workshop live via DO and polling fallback with Promote/Keep/Discard; invalid human promote showing the same fix_hints; anonymous public page including claim and excluding workshop; exact-ID and lexical search; honest share preview; report/quarantine/appeal/restore; console token last-used, pause/revoke/panic; problem proposal/publish control; quiet review-ready discovery through review and qualifying honors where fixtures allow. CACHE/PRINCIPAL PAIRS: two sponsors, two Fellows, anonymous client and an unlisted problem prove workshop/private material never appears in response bodies, metadata, search, feeds, sitemaps, shared caches, logs, traces, videos, or another sponsor console; correct Vary/cache keys and host-only cookie behavior; revocation races an in-flight view/write. ACCESSIBILITY: keyboard-only critical journeys, focus/error announcement and axe assertions. ARTIFACT SAFETY: Playwright traces/videos/screenshots use synthetic data, redact headers/storage/fragment/token values at capture, disable recording on any non-synthetic/private run, pass the never-log scanner before persistence, and never retain raw harness transcripts or chain-of-thought. Structured steps follow OPS.2a with request/event IDs and cursors so a failed UI assertion correlates to Worker state; failure artifact paths use validated run IDs. DONE: suite green on staging CI; privacy/cache pair is permanent; at least one seeded leak, stale-cache, principal-confusion, accessibility and client-side exception fixture each makes the suite fail; retained artifacts diagnose the step without containing credentials, raw private bodies, or hidden reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Playwright component/helpers test principal fixtures, redacted capture, deterministic waits, failure cleanup, request/event correlation and accessibility assertions. scripts/e2e-human-plane.sh runs the complete staging human journey with real Worker/D1/R2/DO and designated Google test users: onboarding/approval/reduction, directives, live workshop/edit/promote/fallback, public exclusion, search/artifacts/moderation, proposal adoption/publication, quiet review/honors, exact sharing, token/account/transfer recovery and every injected 4xx/409/422/429/5xx. Paired sponsors/Fellows/anonymous plus unlisted/private canaries prove absence from response, cache, metadata, search, feed, sitemap, logs, traces and screenshots; no-JS/keyboard/mobile/axe tests pass. OPS.2a records route/action, synthetic IDs, request/event/cursors, render/cache digests, result/timing/diff; retained artifacts are synthetic/redacted and contain no credentials/private bodies/storage/transcripts or hidden reasoning.

title: Tier 2: fmd export face
description: WHY: Fable lists fmd export as a Tier-2 capability after W10. It is an additional portable face, never a replacement for canonical JSON/GFM or the launch JSONL archive, and must not create a second projection/sanitization path. WHAT: first specify the fmd media type, version, canonical ordering, escaping, pagination/continuation, token/byte budget behavior and mapping from the shared export projection. Preserve total attribution, exact object/statement versions, dispositions/facets, source cursors, omitted reasons, event/checkpoint references and content-control tombstones. JSON stays canonical for machines; unsupported/malformed negotiation returns the standard teaching error. Only public export state is eligible. TESTS: unit tables for every object kind, escaping, optional/unknown fields, tombstone, budget and pagination; golden semantic-parity fixtures compare parsed fmd with canonical JSON and GFM meaning; property tests prove deterministic bytes, stable prefixes, lossless supported-field round trip and no invalid truncation; privacy fixtures prove workshop/private/moderation bytes cannot appear; curl E2E negotiates, paginates and resumes a large problem and receives safe errors. OPS.2a logs format/schema version, public cursor, projection/output digest, bytes/token estimate, item/omission counts and timing, never bodies, queries, private content or credentials. DONE: documentation/examples ship; output is deterministic across processes; semantic parity and privacy suites pass; adding/removing this optional face cannot change canonical projections or write contracts.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/table/property and golden tests cover media type/version, every supported object, canonical ordering, escaping, optional/unknown fields, Unicode/math, pagination/continuation, stable-prefix budgets, item-or-omitted accounting, tombstones, hostile markers, deterministic bytes and lossless supported-field round trips to canonical JSON semantics. scripts/e2e-fmd-export.sh negotiates the optional face from curl, paginates/resumes a large real staging problem, verifies semantic parity with JSON/GFM, ETag/cache behavior, malformed/unsupported teaching errors, and absence of workshop/private/unlisted/moderation canaries. OPS.2a JSONL records format/schema version, public problem/cursor, projection/output/semantic digests, bytes/token estimate, item/omission counts, request ID, status/code, timing and bounded diff; never raw query or bodies, private refs, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or transcripts. This bead cannot alter canonical projections, write contracts or launch requirements.

title: W9: Symposiarch quality + safety
description: WHY: Quality is mechanical, not hortatory, while safety and scientific integrity are distinct tracks with distinct rhetoric, evidence and appeals. This epic is the platform brain for screening, suggestions, review routing, accountable moderation and anti-Goodhart recognition. WHAT: W9.1 structural/Workers-AI screening with ACIP injection taxonomy, contextual aggregation, reproducible policy/model provenance, quarantine-first uncertainty and public-taxonomy/private-pattern boundary; W9.2 no-echo secret/PII scanning with asimp parity; W9.3 integration over separately owned W9.3a reports/appeals/independent-sponsor auto-hide/strikes/slow mode, W9.3b analysis-versus-operational-facilitation dual-use policy and trained-human review, and W9.3c scientific-integrity cases/correction linkage; W9.4 moves/materiality; W9.5 writer slots/observer overflow; W9.6 consequence-and-missing-independence review matchmaking; W9.7 recomputed calibration and chronological honors with no rank/tallies. No role, report threshold, detector, moderator or metadata field moves a scientific disposition by fiat. Agents can report and draft appeals; accountable humans decide appeals. Scientific weakness is never dangerous-content rhetoric; quarantine is not an accusation; policy responses starve attack oracles while contract errors teach. TESTS: each child owns exhaustive positive/negative units, mock-free transition/integration tests and relevant E2E through OPS.2a. Corpus gates preserve valid weird math and hard rejects; moderation matrices cover concurrency, independence, appeals, restoration, strikes, integrity corrections, cache/noindex and provider failure; move/match/calibration fixtures prove no activity/actor/model metric leaks into ranking. Logs retain versions, digests, state/action/event IDs and timing but no raw sensitive payloads, detector details, transcripts or private content. DONE: children close; screening FP under 5 percent and hard-reject FN zero on the versioned corpus; moves fire correctly; every moderation/integrity state is actionable and appealable; W10 red-team and W8 admin journeys pass without oracle, authority, privacy or A10 violations.
acceptance_criteria: All child corpus, unit, property, mock-free transition and E2E requirements in the description pass. Thresholds are evaluated on versioned fixed holdouts; every policy/model/corpus change reruns both must-pass legitimate and must-refuse controls. Concurrency tests cover reports/appeals/restore/strikes and screening/outbox races. scripts/e2e-symposiarch.sh exercises pass/warn/quarantine/reject, report-dont-engage, independent auto-hide, appeal, integrity correction, slow mode, move/match/calibration/honors and provider outage. OPS.2a logs only versions/digests/state/action/event IDs and timing; policy bodies remain oracle-minimal and diagnostics contain no restricted evidence/detector detail. No safety/integrity action moves scientific truth.

title: W8.8 Sharing, review discovery, human texts, and admin integration
description: WHY: These are the remaining public/support surfaces of Agora, but honest sharing, review discovery/honors, and operator administration have distinct owners and security boundaries. This bead is their integration gate, not a single-file grab bag. WHAT: integrate W8.8a exact-status share metadata, W8.8b /reviews and chronological /results, and W8.8c served-text human projections plus thin audited admin into the Next.js shell, authorization model, canonical projections, cache/purge map, navigation, and accessibility system. Cross-surface invariants: agent face remains canonical; no workshop/private bytes in metadata; no public count becomes an actor/model leaderboard; admin detail never enters shared caches; every public claim about status links back to its event/evidence trail. DONE: all three children close; a Playwright journey goes from a quiet review-ready claim to isolated review, qualifying honors event, exact-status share card, and audited moderation repair without any Diptych, cache, authority, or A10 violation.
acceptance_criteria: All three child beads close with unit/golden/accessibility and surface-specific E2E suites green. Playwright scripts/e2e-agora-support-surfaces.sh follows a quiet review-ready claim through matched review, chronological honors eligibility, exact-status share metadata and an authorized moderation repair from anonymous/sponsor/operator views; it checks agent-face semantic parity, no-JS/keyboard/mobile, cache partition/purge, noindex, and forbidden workshop/private/leaderboard/admin bytes. OPS.2a logs revision, route/action, synthetic principal class, public object/event IDs, cursor, projection/render/cache digests, status/code, accessibility result and timing; traces/videos are synthetic/redacted and never contain bodies, case payloads, cookies, tokens, browser storage, policy internals, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: W12.P2 Draft SP4D flagship and frontier slate statements
description: WHY: Famous-problem statement and reference work is long-lead, domain-sensitive, and can proceed before the platform; delaying it until the live problem page exists risks either launch delay or a rushed, unsafe flagship. WHAT: under docs/seed/, prepare the SP4D dossier: canonical smooth 4D Poincare formulation; explicit distinctions from topological/PL and commonly conflated variants; authoritative primary references with anchors; honest motivation; falsifier/settlement conditions; scope/out-of-scope; bounded sub-goals such as Gluck twists and trisection invariants; famous-problem banner and exact no-resolution language; external-expert review requirements; proposed moves and evidence artifacts. Prepare smaller dossiers for the rung-6 slate (Kaplansky zero-divisor post-Gardam, union-closed sets, Erdos-Straus, outstanding three-cubes n, Sendov remaining degrees, lonely-runner small k, BB(6) lower bounds, quantum-channel additivity hunts, and a strictly bounded Navier-Stokes sub-question), recording freshness dates so changing problem status is re-verified before publication. Define rung-7 new-theory template requirements: explicit predictions, consistency checks, and distinction from established theory. DONE: the flagship dossier receives independent mathematical review for formulation/variant accuracy; every reference is anchored; every sub-goal is falsifiable and bounded; the slate is labeled draft and no live/current-status claim is made without a pre-publication refresh. W12.2 owns entry through the real sharpening/guardrail machinery.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is scientific source preparation, not runtime code. A versioned review matrix verifies exact formulation, variant distinctions, source anchors, licenses, falsifier, settlement and no-claim language, bounded subgoals, safety notes, and external-expert requirements for every dossier; automated link, citation-shape, schema, and rendered-face fixture checks run in CI. A dated structured review report records dossier/source digests, reviewer expertise and independence, unresolved questions, corrections, and approval state; it never claims expert validation until the named external review occurs.
