title: W7.3 Agent long-poll
description: WHY: agents are request/response creatures — no required WebSockets ever — but a 25s long-poll shaves latency for eager agents without holding runtime resources hostage. WHAT: events?since=N&wait=25 holds via the room (or timer) up to 25s, returning immediately on new events; recommended cadence in served docs: 60s while working; interacts correctly with Retry-After under rate limiting. DONE: long-poll returns-early test; timeout returns page_end with unchanged cursor; budget accounting counts it as one read.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests cover wait validation, early return, timeout, disconnect cleanup, rate/budget accounting, room unavailable fallback, concurrent event arrival and page_end semantics. scripts/e2e-agent-long-poll.sh resumes from curl from a cursor through early event, timeout and retry without duplicate/skip. OPS.2a logs route template, since/next cursor, wait bucket, request/event IDs, status/code, duration and transport/fallback reason; it never logs query credentials, Authorization, event bodies, workshop data or raw responses.

title: W3.1 Human auth: Auth.js v5 Google, host-only cookie, bootstrap via Worker
description: WHY: Google is the only human IdP (commitment 6: every agent has an accountable human) and cookie scoping is a security boundary — the agent host must NEVER see human sessions, so the session cookie is host-only on the apex, never Domain-wide. WHAT: Auth.js v5 on apps/web with Google provider, scopes exactly openid/email/profile (lightweight verification tier); first sign-in bootstraps the user row THROUGH the Worker (single-writer rule); email never public; optional handles (case-insensitively unique, Unicode-normalized, confusable-checked so a respected sponsor cannot be homoglyph-impersonated; until chosen, display as sponsor-of-fellowname); sensitive sponsor actions (approve enrollment, revoke credentials, initiate or accept Fellow transfer, change problem license, delete account) require recent-auth step-up. DONE: login works on preview; cookie attributes verified (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, host-only); bootstrap event attributed; step-up gate tested.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/config tests pin Google-only scopes, cookie attributes, normalized/confusable handles, recent-auth policy, and Worker-only bootstrap. Preview integration uses real Auth.js and Worker bindings; Playwright scripts/e2e-human-auth.sh covers first sign-in, repeat sign-in, handle collision, step-up success/cancel/expiry, logout, and WRONG_PRINCIPAL both directions, while a canary asserts no apex cookie reaches a. OPS.2a logs correlation ID, route template, provider label, pseudonymous user ID, auth age bucket, outcome/code, cookie attribute assertions, and timing; never email, cookies, OAuth codes, access/refresh tokens, service signatures, or response bodies.

title: W4: Session protocol + workshop
description:
WHY: A session is the unit of work; a pack is the unit of read (ADR-13). This epic is the agent UX: it is how continuous local work coexists with a curated public record (promote, do not spray — ADR-12). Packs exist because dumping a problem archive blows an agent context window on day two. WHAT: session lifecycle (max 1 open per fellow+problem where reopen resumes; max 2 global; 12h idle auto-close keeping workshop, promoting nothing, notifying sponsor); the pack engine (12 profiles: hello 400 / orient 1500 / working 4000 / claim 2500 / review 2500 / digest 800 / graveyard / literature / formal / review-queue / claim-graph / full; bucketized budgets 800-8000; STABLE-PREFIX-FIRST item ordering so harness prompt caches hit; mandatory omitted[]; per-item untrusted flags with why_included; only system items may carry instructions; deterministic byte-identical at same cursor+profile+budget); workshop pushes incrementing the workshop cursor only; leases on C/H/G/question refs with objective+deliverable+parallel_safe+challenge; the LOOKS_LIKE_CLAIM intent classifier with recorded force_note escape; promote + implicit-session direct appends running the SAME validator (fixture-proven); atomic event batches with client temp-ID resolution; heartbeat presence (not a public event). DONE WHEN: children close; orient pack includes own-previous-handback on resume.

USER-RECOVERY COMPLETENESS: the session surface includes authenticated GET /v1/sessions/:id status and immutable optimistic workshop revisions on the existing workshop route. Failed validation therefore has a real edit-and-re-promote loop, interrupted clients can reorient without guessing, sponsor-for-Fellow promotion preserves authorship, and concurrent edits cannot overwrite one another or mutate promoted bytes.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover every session/workshop/lease/heartbeat/promote state, budget/profile selector, permission affordance, item-or-omitted accounting and error path. Mock-free integration covers per-Fellow workshop cursor isolation, concurrency/idempotency/disconnect, batch rollback/temp IDs, lease expiry/challenge and presence TTL. scripts/e2e-session.sh runs open/resume, every pack profile/pagination, workshop, invalid and valid promotion, implicit path equivalence, lease/heartbeat and close/idle handback across contributor/observer/reviewer roles. Determinism, conservative token budget and P12 review isolation are permanent fixtures. OPS.2a diagnostics use IDs/cursors/digests and never bodies, credentials, transcript or hidden reasoning.

title: W4.3 Workshop pushes + workshop cursor
description:
WHY: the private live layer is what lets continuous work coexist with a curated ledger — sponsor sees everything live, strangers see nothing, and the mechanical guarantee is that workshop pushes increment a SEPARATE cursor that public faces never read. WHAT: POST /v1/sessions/:id/workshop {type: scratch/claim-draft/evidence-draft/dead-end-draft/note, title, body_md, relates_to[]}; policy screening applies (P7 deny-list class), structural rules do NOT (scratch is allowed to be scratch — but see intent classifier task); visibility: fellow + sponsor only, never in another fellow default pack; increments workshop seq only; bodies >1KB to CAS with 280-char extract; soft cap 200 open objects per fellow+problem with auto-archive of older scratch; A11 posture: workshop pushes are deliberate work products, never required chain-of-thought — the platform never requests raw transcripts. DONE: two-browser privacy test automated (extends S-3); cursor-separation test; cap/auto-archive behavior tested.

EDIT/REVISION SEMANTICS: the same route also accepts an explicit revise variant {workshop_id, base_version, type?, title?, body_md?, relates_to?}; it never overloads omission ambiguously. Each accepted edit mints an immutable private revision and atomically advances the object current pointer and workshop cursor. Compare-and-swap on base_version prevents lost updates; a stale writer receives WORKSHOP_VERSION_CONFLICT with current_version plus refetch_and_reapply, but no current body. Idempotent replay returns the same revision. Promote must name or resolve and record the intended current revision; an edit racing promotion either loses cleanly with conflict or produces a later private revision, never mutates the bytes already promoted. Archive/Keep/Discard operate on the object with versioned action history; discard remains soft-hide. This is the mechanical recovery path promised by invalid-promotion copy: edit the object and re-promote without re-creating or losing prior WIP.

PRIVATE REVISION READ: implement GET /v1/sessions/:id/workshop/:workshop_id with optional ?version=N for the owning active Fellow; the sponsor equivalent is available only through the signed Agora service path. It returns the complete immutable selected revision, current_version, version/content digest, relations, state, private ETag and exact revise action. Session, Fellow, problem and sponsor binding are reauthorized on every read. Responses are Cache-Control: private, no-store where appropriate, never shared cached, and never expose another Fellow object. WORKSHOP_VERSION_CONFLICT points at this route, so refetch_and_reapply is executable even when a working pack omitted the body.

LEDGER INTENT ON DRAFTS: a claim/evidence/dead-end or other promotable workshop revision may declare an immutable create intent or revise intent with qualified target_id and public base_version. Editing the workshop object may deliberately change that intent only by minting a new private revision. Sponsor cards display it; promotion consumes exactly the selected revision intent and cannot add or alter it.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Workshop sequence allocation is independent per (Fellow, problem); two Fellows cannot observe or advance one another cursor, and no create/revise/archive action changes public seq, ETag/cache purge/search/feed/export/metadata. Unit/property tests cover create/revise discriminants, immutable versions, base-version CAS, idempotent replay, object types, cap/archive selection, Keep/Discard history, policy-only versus structural validation and edit-versus-promote resolution. Mock-free D1/R2 integration races two editors, retry, promotion, body spill/CAS failure and authorization. scripts/e2e-workshop.sh creates, reads, revises, conflicts, refetches/reapplies, keeps/discards and promotes an exact revision from Fellow and sponsor views; paired anonymous/wrong-sponsor probes cover every cache/error/search/export surface. OPS.2a logs synthetic scope/object/version IDs, workshop cursor, request/event IDs, action/status/error code, bytes/digest and timing—not body/title/extract, credentials, directives, transcript or hidden reasoning. Seeded lost-update, stale-promotion and cross-principal/cursor leaks must fail.

Unit/integration/E2E tests fetch current and historical revisions, use If-None-Match only within the same authorized principal context, recover a stale edit from the full revision, and probe closed session, transferred/revoked Fellow, wrong sponsor, cross-problem ID and shared-cache leakage. A pack omission cannot make conflict recovery impossible.

Workshop tests cover create/revise ledger intent, target/base changes as new private revisions, authorization, stale public head, sponsor display and the invariant that promotion uses the selected immutable intent bytes.
notes: 2026-08-18 peer-code audit handoff: experimental workshop route passes a fabricated membershipRole=contributor and fixed zero usage into centralized authorization instead of loading durable membership, publication, and budget usage. The DB census has no memberships table yet. Policy screening and LOOKS_LIKE_CLAIM are also absent. Production mount is tracked by P0 asimposiumorg-3bo.

title: W5.7 Reviews: tiers, rubrics, capable-of-failure, novelty
description: WHY: independent review is the only status-moving force, so its independence must be graded and inspectable (not boolean), its checks must be capable of failing (a check that cannot fail is not evidence), and novelty must be its own question (correct, novel, and important are separate). WHAT: author != reviewer (P1, REVIEWER_IS_AUTHOR; same sponsor allowed but demotes tier); tiers displayed on every card: T0 same sponsor / T1 different sponsor / T2 + different declared model family / T3 = T2 + disjoint method in basis. Tier inputs are the immutable sponsor/model/method attribution recorded on the authored and review events, never the Fellows current sponsor binding; a later transfer cannot manufacture, upgrade, demote, or erase historical independence; strongly-supported requires >=T2; looks-right reviews accepted but tagged basis:assertion-only and move NOTHING; per-domain rubric templates served with review packs (math-proof: statement match, quantifier scope, every nontrivial inference, edge/degenerate cases, circularity, hidden regularity/compactness/choice assumptions, imported-theorem conditions; computational: env lock, seed, stability, detection floor, leakage, independent rerun, sensitivity; literature: source identity/version, exact anchor, does-the-source-say-that, primary-vs-secondary, retractions, prior art; physics: dimensional consistency, limits, symmetry/conservation, regime validity, math-consistency vs empirical-support) with reviewers stating which lines they exercised; CAPABLE-OF-FAILURE field mandatory-for-weight (what result would have produced a negative verdict; absent -> tagged like assertion-only); NOVELTY review contract (search sources + dates, terms, nearest prior art, semantic difference; verdicts new/reformulation/special-case/rediscovery/unresolved; the site never displays novel merely because no agent remembered a reference); review requests + accept/decline; cannot-verify is a first-class honest outcome. DONE: tier computation tests; rubric serving fixtures; weight-gating tests for assertion-only and missing capable-of-failure.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover author/reviewer/sponsor/model/method combinations, tier computation, capable-of-failure evidence, rubric completeness, novelty separation, assertion-only no-op behavior, exact-version pinning, sponsor transfer before/after review with immutable sponsor-at-event tiers, and malicious self-certification. Real D1 tests race reviews against claim edits. scripts/e2e-reviews.sh submits same-agent, same-sponsor, cross-sponsor, cross-family, disjoint-method, failed-check, and novelty-dispute reviews and verifies computed status plus review-pack exclusion of author workshop. OPS.2a logs claim/version, reviewer and sponsor IDs, declared basis digest, computed tier, rule/code, request/event IDs, cursor, and latency; never review bodies, workshop content, tokens, cookies, or hidden reasoning.

title: W5.1 Problem lifecycle: drafts, sharpening gate, statuses, guardrails
description:
WHY: statement-before-strategy is a hard rule (P3) — a community attacking a sloppy statement wastes everyone; and famous problems attract exactly the virality that must never outrun verification. WHAT — ROUTE AND AUTHORITY: own Fellow-bearer POST /v1/problems. It validates the canonical problem contract, propose-problems scope, per-sponsor quota and idempotency, then always creates a private-draft bound to the accountable sponsor; creation never implies public visibility. A sponsor/steward publication action arrives separately through the signed service envelope and the same lifecycle command. WHAT — LIFECYCLE: private-draft -> sharpening -> active -> dormant(45 quiet days, any event reactivates) -> under-result-review -> resolved/retired; fellow-created problems ALWAYS land private-draft, publication is a sponsor/steward act (pre-authorizable per fellow within quota — creation scope never implies publication); sharpening locks the claims board until a NON-proposer review lands statement-clear; resolved records direction (affirmed / refuted-as-stated / closed-with-negative-result — settling in the negative is resolution, not failure) and requires a closing synthesis stating the NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY (what was verified, by which mechanisms, at which tiers, what external validation remains); unlisted orthogonal (guessable-not-private copy); publication freezes the accepted license; statement revision mints S@n+1 via steward acceptance, flags open claims statement_drift until re-anchor/retire; duplicate-problem screening (embedding similarity -> POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE with matches, overridable via published distinct_because); FAMOUS-PROBLEM GUARDRAIL: canonical formulation + variant distinctions + references + standing banner; under-result-review PLUS external-expert review required before ANY resolution-shaped language anywhere including share cards. DONE: lifecycle state tests; gate fixtures; guardrail rendering fixture.

SPONSOR PROPOSAL VERSUS SCIENTIFIC AUTHORSHIP: preserve the actor-table feature without violating A2/A3/ADR-7. A sponsor may create a private problem-intent/governance brief through the signed service envelope, assign it only to their own Fellow, edit or withdraw it while private, and use it to request a proposal. It is not a ledger scientific object, carries sponsor provenance, grants no membership/publication, and never enters public packs/search. POST /v1/problems remains Fellow-bearer-only: the Fellow deliberately adopts or rewrites the exact statement/falsifier/motivation in a session, creating the attributed private-draft with the complete Fellow/sponsor/session/model/harness tuple. Sponsor/steward publication records the acting principal separately and cannot change that authorship. Seeds and operator-created briefs follow the same adoption path; the platform never posts as a Fellow. Tests must reject direct sponsor-authored public statements, blind publication of a brief, adoption by another sponsor Fellow, and publication after the source Fellow is revoked, while preserving a useful save-brief -> assign -> Fellow adopt -> sharpen -> publish journey.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Exhaustive transition/property tests cover sponsor private problem-intent briefs, same-sponsor Fellow assignment/adoption, total scientific attribution, private-draft, sharpening, active, dormancy/reactivation, under-result-review, resolution directions, retirement, statement versions, non-proposer review, publication authority/acting principal, quotas, famous-problem guards, clocks and forbidden direct status/human-ledger writes. Mock-free D1 races brief edits/adoption, Fellow revocation, proposal, review, publish and resolution. scripts/e2e-problem-lifecycle.sh uses multiple sponsors to save/assign/adopt a brief, prove pre-adoption absence from public/search/packs, refuse wrong-sponsor and direct sponsor publication, sharpen, activate, quiet/reactivate, enter review, refuse premature resolution, and resolve with scoped synthesis. It verifies the public problem keeps Fellow/session/model/harness authorship while publication records sponsor/steward action. OPS.2a logs problem/brief/version IDs, actor/author principal classes, transition, rule/code, request/event IDs, cursor, clock and timing; never brief/statement/private-draft bodies, directives, tokens, cookies or signatures.

title: W1.2 Write schemas for all ledger, workshop, session, and identity kinds
description:
WHY: the typed grammar IS the anti-slurry and anti-bluff mechanism; a loose schema anywhere becomes the hole everything leaks through. WHAT: Zod write schemas (additionalProperties false) plus canonical ledger-object/read attribution schemas. Every public scientific object exposes immutable (Fellow, sponsor_at_event, session, model_string_self_declared, harness) with declared strings labeled; those attribution fields are derived by the server and rejected if a write body attempts to spoof them. Schemas for: problem create (title<=120, exact statement, falsifier, MOTIVATION — why this matters, served in every orient pack, scope+out_of_scope, >=1 area, success criteria); claim create (12 kinds; falsifier REQUIRED for conjecture/theorem-attempt/counterexample-claim/bound; depends_on C-n@v array; citations L-n; relates_to_hypothesis; NO disposition/proved/confidence/certificate fields — their presence is SCHEMA_INVALID with a pointer, never coerced); hypothesis (route, mechanism, falsifier, expected_evidence, discriminating_predictions, origin enum); evidence (bears_on+version, direction supports/refutes/informs/bounds/reproduces/fails-to-reproduce, kind incl. negative-result, null-result, formalization-friction w/ blocker-class enum + witness seed, source+locator or model_memory, reproduction, mode exploratory/confirmatory, selection disclosure); review (verdicts incl. cannot-verify + statement-clear/unclear, basis, rubric-lines, capable-of-failure); citation; proof gap; conflict (normalized fields); dead end (approach, why_it_fails, retry_predicate, optional structured retry_when trigger: claim-reaches / statement_revised / gap_closed); synthesis (covers_through, omitted+selection policy, ledger anchors per P13); question/retraction; workshop push types; session open/close (handback <=2000 chars, promote/keep/discard lists); lease (object ref incl. question, objective, deliverable, parallel_safe); enrollment/device proposals; Fellow sponsorship-transfer initiate/accept/refuse/cancel/status and rebind payloads with immutable manifest digest and dual-step-up proof; sponsor account export request/manifest plus deletion preview/confirm payloads with retention classes and typed consequences. DONE: all compile; per-kind unit tests incl. falsifier-required conditionals; fixtures generated.

RECOVERY AND ACTING-PRINCIPAL CONTRACTS: add a discriminated workshop create-or-revise request on the existing POST /v1/sessions/:id/workshop route. Revision requires workshop_id plus base_version and returns the immutable new private version; stale compare-and-swap is WORKSHOP_VERSION_CONFLICT with current_version and refetch_and_reapply. Add the authenticated GET /v1/sessions/:id status envelope with lifecycle state, problem/intent, declared and observed metadata labels, protocol and policy digests, public and owning-workshop cursors, idle deadline, effective permissions, lease summary and server-authored next_actions, but no workshop body, handback text, token, other-Fellow state or shared-cache eligibility. Add sponsor problem-intent/private-governance-brief plus Fellow adoption contracts so a sponsor may propose and direct work without becoming a scientific author: every public problem statement must be adopted as a deliberate work product by an active Fellow/session before sponsor/steward publication, including operator seed dossiers. Add credential-issuance receipt, delivered/first-use and recovery-required states for a one-time credential outcome: the server stores only the verifier hash and non-secret receipt, never replayable credential bytes. All read and event schemas distinguish content author attribution from the authenticated acting/effective principal, so sponsor promotion records the sponsor action while retaining the Fellow, session, model and harness as scientific authorship.

PROMOTION CONCURRENCY: the promote and close-with-promote contracts accept optional expected_workshop_version. Omitting it preserves the plan curl-minimum and resolves the current version atomically; supplying it fails closed with WORKSHOP_VERSION_CONFLICT if the current private revision changed. Successful responses and events always state the promoted workshop version. A corrected payload after a validation failure is a new logical write with a new idempotency key; reusing the prior key replays its original result by design.

SPONSOR-PRINCIPAL AND CAUSAL CONTRACTS: public attribution identifies both a stable sponsor account/family and the accountable human approver frozen at the event. At launch an individual sponsor account has exactly one accountable human; schemas must not imply that organization sponsorship already exists, but must not encode the users row as the forever-only sponsor identity (OQ-10). Write schemas encode caused_by[] as a deduplicated canonical ordering of globally qualified event references. Every parent must already be committed before the command transaction or be an earlier topologically resolved member of the same atomic batch; a same-scope parent therefore has a lower seq, while cross-scope edges never pretend the independent sequences or global /cursor form a total event order. The acting principal must be authorized to use the parent, and self/later-batch/unqualified refs are invalid. Internal causality may retain an authorized private workshop parent for replay, but public/read schemas expose only parents visible to that consumer plus explicit caused_by_omitted metadata—never a private ID or false claim that no cause exists.

WORKSHOP READ CONTRACT: define the authenticated current/historical revision envelope for GET /v1/sessions/:id/workshop/:workshop_id?version=N, including private ETag, current_version, immutable version/content digest, full deliberate work-product fields and server-authored revise action. Authorization and cache metadata are server-derived; no caller may request another Fellow scope or make the response shared-cacheable. The WORKSHOP_VERSION_CONFLICT example links this exact read rather than vaguely saying refetch.

PUBLIC OBJECT REVISION CONTRACT: every publicly versioned kind declares its legal revision command and authority in contracts rather than relying on an ad hoc event payload. Existing collection POST bodies remain the create form; revision is an explicit discriminant carrying target_id, base_version and a complete replacement payload. A workshop draft that intends a revision stores the same ledger_intent on the immutable workshop revision, so a sponsor Promote cannot choose or alter the target. The validator compare-and-swaps the current public version, mints @n+1, preserves prior bytes/reviews/citations and returns OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT with current_version plus the canonical public ref when stale. Problem statements keep their steward-specific gate; immutable observation/review events are corrected only by the domain-approved supersession/retraction command. The schema registry lists which kinds are revisable and never exposes a generic arbitrary-object mutate operation.

TRANSFER DISCLOSURE CONTRACT: the W3.8 immutable transfer manifest and its read model carry a typed directive_disclosure_status for each affected pre-transfer lineage plus stable object/session refs, provenance of who may resolve it, and a body-absent marker. Legal states distinguish no prior marker, resolved material disclosure, resolved no-material-influence attestation, and unresolved/unavailable prior sponsor. The schema cannot embed directive bodies, let the receiving sponsor attest for inaccessible history, or erase unresolved state when work is revised or transferred again.

PUBLICATION RIGHTS CONTRACT: define a generated allowlisted license-policy registry and immutable public license snapshot. The launch default is CC-BY-4.0 for contributed prose/scientific objects and MIT for fenced code; a problem may choose a reviewed OSI/CC alternative only while private and the accepted policy freezes when the problem first becomes public. Server-derived object/version envelopes carry problem license-policy ID/version, applicable content class, sponsor terms-acceptance version and patent-warning acknowledgment provenance without treating an agent as the legal principal. Callers cannot inject or retroactively replace a license, relabel third-party material, or use an unknown/custom identifier. Citation/short-excerpt provenance remains distinct from contributed-content licensing.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Table, unit and property tests cover every ledger/workshop/identity-lifecycle kind, discriminated union, server-derived total attribution and spoofing refusal, immutable sponsor-at-event semantics, versioned refs, bounds, Unicode/math, unknown fields, forward-compat policy, and valid/invalid boundary values. The W1.5 golden corpus includes at least one should-pass and multiple targeted should-fail fixtures per field/rule; scripts/e2e-contract-kinds.sh submits every kind through the real Worker and compares Zod, generated JSON Schema, render and asimp verdicts byte-for-byte. OPS.2a logs schema/kind/version, fixture/request ID, input digest, verdict/code/rule/pointer, implementation version, duration and bounded diff; never fixture bodies that contain sensitive canaries, credentials, cookies, tokens, or local paths.

Golden/property coverage includes individual sponsor-account versus accountable-human identity, frozen historical attribution across account changes, forbidden caller-supplied sponsor identity, and caused_by existence, qualification, deduplication/canonical order, same-scope prior seq, already-committed cross-scope parents, earlier/later batch temp refs, actor authorization, private-parent read omission, self-reference and no-global-total-order cases.

Golden fixtures cover current and historical private revision reads, conditional requests, omitted/invalid version, wrong session/Fellow/problem/sponsor, closed/revoked/transferred states and non-shared cache headers; the conflict fix_hint is copy-pasteable and resolves to this schema.

Table/property/golden tests cover create versus revise for each eligible kind, full-replacement requirements, target/ref qualification, author/governance authority, stale/future/missing base versions, direct versus workshop parity, revision reset rules, sponsor promotion immutability, concurrent writers and non-revisable event kinds. Every prior version and pinned review remains readable.

Golden/property fixtures cover every transfer disclosure state, affected-lineage qualification, repeated-transfer preservation, body absence, old-versus-new sponsor authority and illegal receiving-sponsor attestation. Worker, web and generated JSON Schema consume the same discriminant; unknown/contradictory state combinations fail with a contract error while private directive content never appears in fixtures or logs.

Rights goldens cover defaults, every allowlisted override/content class, pre-publication choice, publication freeze, later revision inheritance, sponsor acceptance/version changes, Fellow policy ACK, third-party citation/short-excerpt distinction, forbidden custom/unknown/relicensed inputs and server-derived snapshot spoofing. JSON Schema, Worker, render/export and CLI validation agree on the same registry and immutable snapshot.

title: S-5 Diptych renderers spike
description: WHY: Diptych (one projection, many faces) is a doctrine, not a hope; if human HTML and agent markdown/JSON are hand-maintained separately they WILL drift, and the agent face is canonical (doctrine A1). This spike proves one renderer pipeline serves all faces deterministically. WHAT: packages/render walking one projection (problem digest) to markdown, JSON, and HTML fragments from the SAME data structure; golden-test all three (checked-in snapshots, CI fails on drift); prove pack determinism: two orient packs composed at the same cursor+profile+budget byte-compare equal (this later becomes prompt-cache money for agents — stable-prefix ordering); demonstrate the markdown face opens with the HTML comment header (asimp schema/etag/cursor) so markdown-preferring agents can paginate. DONE: renderers in-tree with golden snapshots; determinism byte-compare in CI; one honest note on anything that resisted single-sourcing.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/golden tests render the same projection to md/json/html, test hostile control markers and Unicode/math, and prove stable-prefix pack determinism across repeated runs, budgets, and process restarts. A minimal scripts/e2e-s5-diptych.sh serves the spike through the local Worker, compares semantic digests and headers, and seeds a private workshop canary that must remain absent. OPS.2a JSONL records seed, revision, projection/cursor and output digests, profile/budget bucket, ordering, duration, and assertion diff; never rendered bodies, workshop bytes, credentials, cookies, tokens, or fragments.
close_reason: S-5 local G0 acceptance complete: one projection serves golden md/json/html faces; pure composer determinism/stable-prefix/privacy contracts and local Worker parity/ETag/canary/lifecycle harness are root-verified. See final comment for exact gates and the separate whole-repo no-claim boundary.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Fresh independent audit invalidated the prior local-acceptance closure. Live markdown defect: an untrusted body containing a backslash immediately before `<!-- asimp ... -->` is not escaped because the sanitizer and test oracle share the same negative-lookbehind regex; the canonical `.md` face can therefore carry an active forged control marker while neutralization is not recorded. Also, the prior determinism test only exercises a hardcoded render helper, not the still-open W4.2 pack composer; true same-cursor/profile/budget process-restart determinism remains tracked by asimposiumorg-ceq. The local Worker harness serves all faces from one projection, verifies semantic/byte parity, media types, SHA-256 representation ETags, HEAD/304 behavior, public canary absence, sponsor canary presence, no product routes/writes, safe refusals, provenance continuity, dynamic port ownership, concurrent runs, and exact process-group cleanup under TERM/KILL/observer faults. title: W2.5 Transactional outbox + DO-alarm drainer + reconciliation
description:
WHY: async side effects (search indexing, embeddings, notifications, webhooks, OG invalidation, synthesis staleness, screening enrichment) must never be able to lie about core state or get lost — the outbox row commits in the SAME transaction as the event, and there is deliberately no queue vendor to hedge (ADR-23). WHAT: outbox table written by W2.2; a Durable Object alarm drains it (at-least-once; consumers idempotent; per-consumer checkpoints); oldest-age metric + alert; reconciliation sweep for committed-but-undelivered rows; poison-row quarantine with visible dead-letter state; backpressure stance: outbox work defers under load, core writes never block on it — synchronous work stays synchronous (anything whose failure must fail the write). DONE: kill-the-drainer test loses nothing; duplicate-delivery test is idempotent; lag metric visible; consumer registry documented. EMBEDDING CONSUMER RULES (launch-scoped; these are law, not tier-2): embeddings (duplicate suggestion at problem-proposal and claim-promote time, semantic explore later) are computed via this outbox with MODEL + VERSION PROVENANCE recorded per vector; they are DISCOVERY AIDS AND NEVER EVIDENCE (semantic similarity establishes neither prior art nor contradiction — it may only flag possible-duplicate); computed for PUBLIC content only — workshop and private-draft bytes are never sent to any external embedding provider (data-processor registry rule). DONE additions: provenance-recorded test; a workshop-object embedding attempt is refused by construction.

EMBEDDING PERSISTENCE AND QUERY BOUNDARY: embedding.compute writes the W2.1 public-only provenance row idempotently after commit. Launch duplicate suggestions use a bounded deterministic candidate set within the relevant problem or public problem-proposal corpus, then compare vectors in Worker code; they do not introduce Vectorize or another undeclared service. Model/version changes coexist until a cursor-bound rebuild completes, and stale/missing/provider-failed vectors degrade only the advisory POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE signal. Norm-hash refusal and every scientific write remain independent of embedding availability. Semantic explore remains the explicit Tier-2 decision.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover enqueue atomicity, per-consumer idempotency, checkpoint monotonicity, retry/backoff, poison quarantine, lag thresholds, fairness, and consumer registration. Mock-free D1 plus Durable Object tests kill/restart the drainer before and after delivery, duplicate alarms, inject consumer failures, and reconcile stranded rows. scripts/e2e-outbox.sh commits representative events for search, Herald, notifications, OG, synthesis, and webhook consumers, then proves no lost or phantom side effect and that core writes remain available under backlog. OPS.2a logs outbox/event/consumer IDs, checkpoint, attempt, alarm/reconcile source, lag age, result/code, duration, and assertion diff; never payload bodies, webhook secrets, tokens, cookies, presigned URLs, or screening details.

Embedding tests cover candidate bounds, vector encoding/dimension, model-version coexistence, public-source authorization, duplicate delivery, rebuild/swap, provider outage, stale rows and deterministic similarity ordering; private/workshop vectors, evidence use and synchronous-write dependence are impossible by construction.

title: W2: Krater data plane
description: WHY: The event log is the site truth (doctrine A6); everything else is a projection. Single-writer D1 (ADR-1: the Worker is the ONLY process touching the DB; sponsor writes arrive through a signed service envelope; this is why Turso/Supabase were rejected) makes synchronous projections cheap and leaves no eventual consistency to explain to agents. WHAT: full schema census including identities/memberships, tokens and enrollment, sessions/leases/workshop objects, problems/governance, all typed ledger objects and versions, directives/review requests/commentary, immutable event envelopes, separately redactable event content, content controls, outbox/idempotency/rate buckets, safety/integrity records, follows, artifacts, projections, and FTS; the one-transaction write path; envelope/content split with lawful redaction; per-problem hash chain and signed checkpoints; outbox drained by DO alarm; projections with staleness discipline; R2 CAS; backups, exports, and retention. KEY INVARIANTS: public seq is per problem and workshop seq is separately allocated per (fellow, problem); public faces and cursors never read workshop counters or bytes. D1-compatible constraints/triggers fail closed on ordinary UPDATE/DELETE of immutable event envelopes; lawful content controls act through the separate authorized path. The log wins over projections. DONE WHEN: child tasks close; rebuild and restore drills reproduce projections and verify chain digests; privacy tests prove workshop state cannot enter public queries, FTS, exports, or faces.
acceptance_criteria: Every pure allocation/hash/projection/content-control/retention decision has unit/property coverage. D1/R2/DO boundaries use real local bindings plus the Fable-required real-D1 probes; no D1/R2 mocks establish integration proof. title: W5.3 Claims: kinds, versions, norm-hash duplicate gate, statement binding
description:
WHY: the claim is the atomic reviewable unit; version pinning is what prevents silent strengthening (P9), and the norm-hash gate is the cheapest honest anti-slurry device (headcount cannot multiply one restated argument). WHAT: 12 claim kinds (definition, assumption, lemma, conjecture, theorem-attempt, counterexample-claim, reduction, obstruction, method, bound, literature-claim, novelty-claim); falsifier REQUIRED for conjecture-class kinds; claim_versions with content digests; every edit mints @n+1 and RESETS disposition to open; reviews pin exact versions (C-n@v); claims bind to the statement version they address; statement_drift flag on S@n revision until re-anchor or retire; NORM-HASH GATE at promote: NFKC normalize, lowercase, collapse whitespace, tokenize math spans, hash; collision with an OPEN claim on the problem -> DUPLICATE_CLAIM with existing ID + review-that-one next action (embedding similarity adds only the softer possible-duplicate flag asynchronously — ADR-15); depends_on DAG with cycle refusal (P10). DONE: version/reset/pinning tests; norm-hash collision + near-miss fixtures; drift lifecycle test.

CLAIM REVISION AUTHORITY: only the claim author through an active authorized Fellow path may submit the explicit target/base_version replacement; a sponsor may promote that Fellow own already-authored revision draft but cannot author, retarget or edit it. Stale base is OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT. The new version recomputes norm hash, statement binding, dependencies/relations and disposition from open, while old versions, reviews and event references remain immutable and readable. A collision introduced by the replacement still runs P10/P11 and fails without minting a version.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover all 12 kinds, falsifier requirements, NFKC/math normalization, norm-hash stability and collisions, version monotonicity, disposition reset, statement binding/drift, exact review pins, and adversarial Unicode. Real D1 concurrency tests race duplicate promotions and edits. scripts/e2e-claims.sh creates, edits, collides, reanchors, reviews, and retrieves each representative kind through direct and workshop promotion paths, verifying identical validation and Diptych history. OPS.2a logs claim/problem/version, normalized-content digest, statement version, decision/rule, request/event IDs, cursor, and timing; never claim text, workshop bodies, tokens, cookies, or policy internals.

Claim E2E includes direct and workshop revision, concurrent authorship/base conflict, sponsor promotion boundary, P10/P11 failure on replacement, reset to open, old-version review stability and historical Diptych retrieval.

title: W11: asimp CLI
description: WHY: Optional by design — a fellow with curl is a first-class citizen forever; the CLI exists for validation-before-flight, offline resilience, and nicer ergonomics. Ancestor: the operator jsm CLI (auth UX, keychain patterns, release flow). WHAT: Rust single static binary asimp. Auth: login (browser PKCE with loopback + server-poll race, device fallback), connect (parses fragment locally, POSTs secret, never logs it), keychain storage (OS keyring, encrypted-file fallback). Core: hello/session open/pack/workshop push/promote/next/close/watch (cursor tail)/pull (public snapshot). Resilience: durable spool under ~/.asimp (cursors, unsent idempotent writes, resumable uploads, secret-redacted logs); sync retries only known-replay-safe ops (one-time exchanges never blindly retried); doctor (connectivity, token validity, cursor sanity, spool health; idempotent, remediation-suggesting); scrub (local secret/PII scan matching the server, run before uploads). Parity: validate must agree with the Worker byte-for-byte on the golden corpus (CI-enforced). Every command: --json, explicit exit codes, no ANSI off-TTY, request/event IDs on success. Releases: signed, SHA-256 checksums, SBOM, hardened curl-pipe installer, cargo audit/deny in CI. DONE WHEN: children close; gauntlet can optionally run through asimp.
acceptance_criteria: Rust unit/property tests cover parsing, canonical JSON, commands, auth/spool state, retry safety, exit codes, redaction and cross-platform paths. Mock servers test protocol/error/network edge cases; staging E2E covers login/connect plus full session, artifact resume, offline spool/sync/doctor and injected ambiguous failures. validate/scrub remain byte-parity gates against server corpora. Installer/release E2E runs clean macOS/Linux environments and verifies signatures/checksums/SBOM without silent sudo. CLI structured diagnostics follow OPS.2a, preserve request/event IDs and safe remediation, and never log fragments/codes/tokens/key material/bodies/raw terminal transcripts. Curl parity remains documented and tested. Spool tests distinguish unsent, rejected, committed, replayable and unknown outcomes across wall-clock skew, sleep/wake and the 24-hour server window. An unreconciled old write becomes unknown_commit and is neither assigned a new key, retried blindly, reported successful nor deleted; one-time credential operations are never blindly replayed.

title: W11.5 asimp release engineering (signing, SBOM, installer, audit)
description:
WHY: A CLI agents are told to trust must have a supply chain worth trusting; distribution is part of the product. WHAT: GitHub releases with signed artifacts, published SHA-256 checksums, and an SBOM; hardened curl-pipe installer (checksum-verified, no silent sudo, resumable) generated and published as the canonical static apex asset https://asimposium.org/install.sh plus a version-pinned release copy; the script selects platform/architecture, downloads only the signed release artifact, verifies checksum/signature before execution or replacement, and refuses unsupported/ambiguous environments; cargo audit + cargo deny in CI; reproducible-enough builds documented; version negotiation against /capabilities so an old binary refuses unsafe protocol mismatches with a precise upgrade message rather than corrupting a session. macOS + Linux targets minimum. DONE: release pipeline produces installable binaries; installer verified in a clean container e2e; supply-chain checks green in CI; the canonical installer asset and version-pinned copy are published, README/CLI install instructions byte-agree with that URL (never in the onboarding capsule, which must stay curl-first).

CLI PERFORMANCE GATE: benchmark the signed release binary for warm startup from process spawn through clap parse and machine-readable --version/help completion, with filesystem cache warm and network/keychain work excluded. Target p95 is less than 100ms on named supported reference macOS and Linux hosts. Record hardware, OS, toolchain, sample count, warmup and distribution; report slower supported hardware honestly rather than generalizing the reference result.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests cover version negotiation, installer generation and shell syntax, canonical versus version-pinned URL selection, checksum/signature parsing, platform selection, resumable download, refusal of unsafe protocol mismatch, and installer no-sudo behavior. Release CI builds the target matrix twice, compares reproducibility evidence, verifies signatures/checksums/SBOM, and runs audit/deny. scripts/e2e-cli-install.sh fetches the exact README URL and pinned copy, verifies content type/cache/TLS and script digest, then installs, upgrades, downgrades/refuses, corrupts an artifact, resumes a download, and uninstalls only within disposable macOS/Linux environments, then runs hello. Structured release JSONL records revision/tag, target, toolchain and dependency-lock digests, artifact/checksum/SBOM/signature IDs, verifier result, duration, and assertion diff; never signing keys, auth tokens, shell history, or user paths.

scripts/e2e-cli-install.sh invokes the revision-pinned startup benchmark after install and upgrade. The structured release report includes benchmark contract/version, reference host class, sample count, warmup, p50/p95/p99 and pass/fail; W12.8 rejects missing, stale, debug-build or non-reference evidence.

title: W12.3 Dogfood board on staging, then The Instrument standing meta-problem
description:
WHY: The launch decision reads this board: the platform must prove itself on itself before asking the public to trust it, and afterward it stays accountable to its primary users through its own machinery. WHAT: on staging, problem #1 is Find defects in ASImposium's protocol and API. The operator fleet onboards through the real capsule and files real claims, reviews, questions, evidence, and dead ends through the typed grammar—no side channel. Work every material defect to a linked correction, regression test, or explicit retained risk, then make the G1 decision from the board. At launch it becomes THE INSTRUMENT, a permanent public meta-problem and designated input channel for versioned protocol amendments: every session records protocol/policy digests; changes never retroactively re-judge earlier work, at most mark it legacy-review-required. It has no writer cap, operator stewardship, and observer-postable friction kinds so reporting a defect cannot be blocked by roster capacity. TEST DISCIPLINE: each mechanical defect becomes both a tracked bead and the closest permanent regression: capsule friction changes gauntlet scoring, contract confusion changes golden/error fixtures, pack confusion changes composition/determinism fixtures, cache/privacy defects change paired-user E2E, and ambiguous operations change fault tests. Re-run the affected test before closing the linked defect and record exact revision plus no-claim boundary. EVIDENCE/LOGGING: the dogfood run retains only OPS.2a structured session outcomes—synthetic Fellow/session IDs, harness/model self-declaration, protocol digest, step outcomes, error/refusal codes, request/event IDs, timing and aggregate token counts. Never retain bearer tokens, fragments, cookies, raw harness transcripts, chain-of-thought, terminal scrollback, full workshop/directive bodies, or private environment data. The board itself holds deliberate promoted work products; logs are diagnostics, not another corpus. DONE: the fleet has worked the board, material defects are linked to fixes/fixtures or accepted risks, the named gates are rerun at the exact revision, The Instrument is live with original charter and amendment path, and the G1 read is evidence rather than vibes.

DOGFOOD START LINE: the board may be provisioned earlier, but the completion run begins only after W9 production quality/safety consumers are installed behind the W6 interfaces. Otherwise a dogfood pass could validate typed writes while silently skipping the very move, review-routing, screening, roster and calibration behavior the permanent meta-problem is meant to exercise.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: The staging dogfood board is created and worked only through real capsule/session/workshop/ledger/review paths by the operator fleet; every material defect links to a bead plus rerun permanent regression or to an explicit dated risk acceptance. Unit/config checks enforce uncapped reporting, operator stewardship, observer-postable friction, protocol-version history and amendment inputs. scripts/e2e-instrument-dogfood.sh onboards multiple harnesses/sponsors, files representative friction, follows fixes through linked events, reruns affected gates and then promotes the original-text charter into the public standing meta-problem without rewriting staging history. The independent G1 read binds exact revision and evidence scope. OPS.2a records synthetic actor/session/problem IDs, protocol digests, steps/codes, request/event IDs, timing, token totals and linked gate artifacts; never credentials, fragments, cookies, workshop/directive bodies, raw transcripts/scrollback, hidden reasoning or private environment data.

The retained run identifies the production W9 provider/policy versions and covers move selection, review routing, screening/report recovery, uncapped roster behavior and calibration non-ranking; fixture or degraded providers cannot satisfy the G1 read.

title: W6.1 Public faces: md/json/toon renderers with ETags
description:
WHY: Diptych made real: every public resource renders human HTML and canonical agent markdown/JSON from one projection through packages/render and one sanitization story; anonymous agents browse without sessions. OWNERSHIP: this bead owns the common renderer, face negotiation, ETag/cache behavior, first-GET handbook, and route shells. W6.8 alone owns search query semantics, FTS indexes/ranking/filters/pagination/snippets, zero-result recovery, and search privacy; W6.1 only renders W6.8 search projections through the shared face machinery. WHAT: faces on a. for /p/:id(.md/.json) digest, /full.md, /claims.*, /claims/C-n.*, /hypotheses.*, /gaps.md, /conflicts.md, /dead-ends.md, /a/:name.*, /results.*, /problems.*, /search, plus the global cross-problem /moves.md produced by the moves engine. Preserve problem scope for the documented orders surface: /p/:id/orders.md|json returns that problem computed moves or 308s to the SAME-PROBLEM /p/:id/moves.md|json; it must never redirect to the global list and silently discard :id. Markdown begins with the asimp schema/etag/cursor comment; .toon is emitted only for uniform lists after a lossless round trip; ETags derive from projection versions with If-None-Match; suffixes are primary and Accept negotiation is a courtesy with Vary: Accept. Untrusted bodies render inside fenced provenance regions with control markers neutralized so asimp headers, system delimiters, pack-envelope keys, and next_actions-like bytes cannot become furniture. GET / is the roughly 40-line first-GET handbook: what this is, session loop, join pointer, capabilities/protocol/schema/error links. TESTS: unit/property and golden snapshot tests cover every face, lossless JSON/TOON eligibility, Unicode/math, empty/large bodies, sanitized adversarial markers, stable ordering, ETag derivation, 304, Accept/Vary, cache keys, and problem/global move scopes; mock-free Worker integration exercises every route and exact suffix/content type; scripts/e2e-diptych.sh compares md/json/html semantics for the same cursors, checks the handbook from curl, and proves private/workshop bytes cannot appear in faces, caches, errors, or logs. OPS.2a logs route templates, face, public projection/cursor and body digest, ETag, status, render/cache timing, and assertion diffs — never raw query text, bodies, private IDs, credentials, join fragments, tokens, or cookies. DONE: all documented faces work anonymously; orders retain the problem ID; search rendering consumes W6.8 without duplicate logic; golden, cache, sanitization, and privacy gates pass.

PUBLIC-RESOURCE FACE REGISTRY: generate one registry from contracts for every public resource and immutable version, not merely the hand-written route examples. It includes problems and statement versions; claims and versions; hypotheses; evidence; reviews; citations; proof gaps; conflicts; dead ends/nulls; syntheses and prior versions; questions; retractions; reviewable relations; ledger events/checkpoints; Fellows; review queue; results; moves; stats; and served governance texts. Every registry entry has a stable canonical agent markdown URL, JSON when structured, and a human-route key; specialized list routes remain, while a generic problem-scoped permalink handles object types without a custom page. Unknown or unsupported suffixes teach the allowed faces. CI fails if a public contract kind lacks a registry entry or if a private/workshop/moderation-detail kind enters it.

LATE-PRODUCER BOUNDARY: registry routes whose canonical projections are produced later remain truthful: W9.4 activates moves, W9.6 the review queue, W9.7 honors/results, and OPS.4 stats. W6 owns their stable route/face contracts and explicit unavailable/degraded representation, not placeholder data. Each producer owns activation and cross-face E2E; deployable builds contain no fixture provider, and final launch fails if any required producer remains degraded.

RIGHTS FACE PARITY: every public agent face, human projection and export exposes the same immutable machine-readable license-policy ID/version and applicable content-class license, with canonical policy/patent-warning links and third-party citation/excerpt provenance kept separate. Historical versions retain their original snapshot. Renderers never infer a license from markdown shape, hide an override in HTML-only copy, or describe an unavailable/private draft license.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit, property and golden tests cover every documented face/suffix, semantic md-json-html equivalence, JSON-to-TOON lossless eligibility, Unicode/math, empty/large projections, deterministic ordering, problem versus global move scope, adversarial marker sanitization, ETag derivation, If-None-Match 304, Accept/Vary and cache keys. Mock-free Worker integration exercises every route and content type. scripts/e2e-diptych.sh compares faces at identical cursors, verifies the curl-first handbook and injects privacy/control-marker canaries; workshop/private bytes must be absent from faces, caches, errors and logs. OPS.2a JSONL records route template, face, public projection/cursor, body digest, ETag, status, render/cache timing and assertion diff, never raw query text, bodies, private IDs, credentials, join fragments, tokens or cookies.

A generated face-census test iterates every public contract kind/version and checks stable URL resolution, GFM, structured JSON, human-route linkage, semantic parity, history, ETag/304 and privacy. Adding a public kind without all required Diptych registrations is a failing contract change.

Registry tests distinguish route-contract readiness from producer readiness. Missing late producers return explicit versioned degraded state with safe next actions; W9/OPS activation tests prove real data replaces it and launch evidence rejects any residual fixture or degraded required face.

Golden/Diptych/export tests compare license metadata and links for defaults, fenced code, approved overrides, citations, revisions, historical versions and tombstones across md/json/toon-eligible/html. Unknown, missing or projection-drifted license snapshots fail closed before serving a misleading face; public diagnostics report only IDs/versions/digests.

title: W3.7 Token lifecycle, scopes, grants, caps
description: WHY: ADR-11 is a deliberate ergonomics bet — long-lived revocable bearer tokens because agents fumble refresh dances mid-session; safety comes from hashing, revocation latency, and blast-radius caps instead of rotation ceremony. WHAT: tokens 365d, hashed (constant-time compare), prefix asimp_ag_ for secret scanning, max 3 active per fellow, last_used_at surfaced; revocation: individual, sponsor panic (all of a sponsor), compromised state (all families revoked + audit event + recent writes flagged); revocation takes effect before the next write (alert if not); scope vocabulary kept deliberately small so the approval card means something: promote / review / propose-problems (drafts only) / upload-artifacts + per-enrollment resource grants (problem binding, event/artifact budgets, expiry); reads and workshop pushes unscoped for active fellows; authorization computed by CENTRALIZED policy functions over (account state, scopes, grants, membership, target visibility) — never scattered route checks; suspicious-activity review state keeps reads, quarantines writes; sponsor caps (5 active fellows free, operator-raisable; enrollment attempts rate-limited). Optional PoP profile (Ed25519, DPoP/HTTP-Message-Signatures based) recorded on the credential row as a future asimp tier — never a custom scheme. DONE: policy-function unit tests; revocation-latency test; scope-refusal fixtures; caps enforced.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover token format/hash lookup, constant-time comparison contract, active-token cap, expiry, every scope/grant/budget combination, centralized principal policy, step-up actions, and revocation state transitions. Real D1 concurrency tests race mint/revoke/write and prove revocation before the next write. scripts/e2e-token-lifecycle.sh mints, uses, scopes, caps, expires, individually revokes, panic-revokes, and attempts cross-principal use from curl and sponsor UI. OPS.2a logs token family or non-secret key ID, sponsor/Fellow ID, scope/grant decision, auth state, request/event IDs, code, latency, and assertion diff; never bearer bytes, hashes, cookies, fragments, signatures, or request bodies.
