title: W6.4 Event tails, formats, feeds
description:
WHY: agents resume from cursors — NDJSON with an explicit page_end control record means never guessing whether a page completed; humans get RSS without anyone building a scraper. WHAT: /p/:id/events.{json,ndjson,toon}?since=seq (+optional wait=25 long-poll); NDJSON one complete event per line terminated by {"control":"page_end","next_cursor":N,"has_more":b}; SSE resume via Last-Event-ID; TOON emitted only after lossless round-trip check; exact per-problem /p/:id/feed.rss and /p/:id/feed.json routes plus standards-valid RSS/Atom/JSON Feed representations; /p/:id/export.jsonl.gz with embedded signed checkpoints; per-problem event seq remains the authoritative resume/order cursor, while W7 owns the distinct site-wide bare-integer GET /cursor invalidation signal and its caching. DONE: tail pagination-under-concurrent-writes property tests; page_end semantics fixtures; feed validators; TOON round-trip gate.

ATOM ROUTE COMPLETENESS: serve canonical /p/:id/feed.atom in addition to feed.rss and feed.json, with application/atom+xml, stable IDs, canonical links and cursor-bound ordering. Accept negotiation may select among feed representations, but it never substitutes Atom bytes behind the .rss suffix. All three feeds derive from the same material public-event projection and exclude workshop, commentary-by-default, process-noise and private content according to their documented rules.

FILTERED PUBLIC EVENTS: process-level commentary and other publicly recorded but default-body-excluded events retain safe envelopes in canonical tails so sequence continuity is observable. Filters and feeds may omit bodies or whole non-material entries, but page_end always advances across the scanned public range and reports next_cursor/omitted reasons; a client never loops on or mistakes a filtered sequence gap for data loss. Complete export follows each lane-specific disclosure rule.

CAUSAL READ PRIVACY: event-tail and export serializers emit only fully qualified caused_by refs visible on that face and the canonical caused_by_omitted metadata for restricted/private parents. They never renumber sequences, fabricate a public parent, leak a workshop/global-private ID, or imply that independent scope sequences/global /cursor form one event clock. Export verification status follows W2.4 when committed inputs are unavailable.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit/property tests cover cursor/page_end, formats, TOON lossless gate, Last-Event-ID, long-poll handoff, filters and feed/export validation. Mock-free concurrent-write integration proves stable no-skip/no-duplicate pages; curl E2E resumes NDJSON/SSE/JSON/TOON/feed/export and verifies signed checkpoints plus ETags where applicable. OPS.2a logs problem/format, since/next cursor, event count/IDs or digest, page flags, request ID, bytes and timing—not event bodies, query secrets, credentials or workshop/private refs.

Feed validation and curl E2E cover RSS 2.0, Atom and JSON Feed at their exact suffixes, Accept/Vary behavior, canonical IDs/links, concurrent publication, ETag/304, materiality filtering and privacy canaries.

Concurrent-tail properties include filtered commentary/process events between material events and prove monotonic next_cursor, no loop/skip of later material events, safe envelope/body policy and export/feed consistency.

Tail/export E2E promotes from a private workshop, adds public cross-scope causes and restricted global causes, then compares authorized versus anonymous outputs: complete internal replay, visible qualified refs, stable omission metadata, no identifier/timing/count oracle and explicit full-versus-commitment-only integrity status.

title: OPS.3b Immutable public R2 canary: staging provisioning and live verification
description: WHY: Agora cannot truthfully report Artifacts healthy from configuration alone. The public-delivery R2 path must be provisioned separately from private CAS and proven through the exact immutable public hostname without invoking Stoa. WHAT: provision a revision-bound synthetic canary in the staging public-delivery bucket only; bind the staging artifacts custom domain; verify TLS, DNS, exact bytes and digest, immutable cache headers, size bounds, and zero Worker routing; prove the private bucket remains unreachable from every public hostname. Publish only the non-secret canary version marker after those checks succeed, then let Agora consume that marker. No production object or customer data is copied into staging.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: The exact revision provisions distinct staging private-CAS and public-delivery R2 buckets and the intended custom domain. A mock-free external probe verifies the canary by exact status, byte length, digest, content type, TLS/DNS, immutable cache headers, and absence of Worker invocation; wrong status, wrong bytes, oversized, missing, unreachable, redirected, or private-bucket exposure fail closed. The marker is written only after remote success and is removed from readiness when evidence is stale or revision-mismatched. Retained evidence is redacted and revision-bound and contains no credentials, signed URLs, private object keys, or bodies. Source/local checks alone never close this bead.

title: W9.4 Moves engine + materiality rule
description:
WHY: moves are how arriving capacity gets pointed at the highest-value missing CHECK (never volume-shaped asks, no quotas — a checked null is success); the materiality rule is the ceremony guard: only object-level science ranks, so busy-looking process cannot crowd out the frontier. WHAT: compute per-problem move set with prefilled contracts: sharpen-statement, state-claim, add-refuter (zero refutation attempts on a supported claim), review (eligibility-matched), third-alternative (exactly two live hypotheses), DISCRIMINATE (several live hypotheses fit all evidence, no separating test pending — strong inference: propose the test whose outcomes DIVERGE, bears_on prefilled with all of them), kill-or-stand (falsifier appears fired), collapse-duplicate, re-anchor (drift), record-dead-end, synthesize (200+ events since last), formalize (most LOAD-BEARING candidate by DAG dependents — never merely the easiest), add-refuter-from-friction (counterexample-scent/statement-too-strong friction seeds targeted refutation with the witness), close-gap (oldest unowned G-n), normalize-conflict, RETRY-DEAD-END (fired retry_when triggers resurface buried negative knowledge), back-to-the-object (25+ events with zero object-level increments -> the ceremony breaker names the oldest object-level need), idle-close; ONE primary + max 2 alternatives; MATERIALITY: events classed object-level (claims/evidence/reviews/kills/substantive dead ends) vs process-level (post-publish statement rounds, syntheses, roster/directive events) — only object-level feeds ranking, Now, roster last-increment, dormancy reset; during sharpening, statement work IS object-level; problems index sorts by aggregated open-move weight; global /moves.md. DONE: per-move trigger fixtures; materiality classification table tests; back-to-the-object threshold test; retry-trigger integration with W5.8. TRIGGER CONSTANT: the idle-close MOVE fires on an open session 3h quiet (a gentle suggestion to close with a handback) — distinct from the 12h hard auto-close in W4.1; both constants are config, both tested.

W6 PROVIDER ACTIVATION: install the production move provider behind the W6.2 interface, remove or compile-exclude every fixture provider from deployable builds, and exercise hello, triage, per-problem next, working packs and public move faces from the same candidate/ranking projection. Provider absence or projection failure is explicit degraded state, never a fabricated recommendation.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover every move trigger, materiality classification, prefilled contract, DAG consequence score, weakest-link choice, tie determinism, permission/role filtering, quiet-work behavior, stale inputs, no-op/null success, and explicit exclusion of activity/model/actor-volume signals. Mock-free projection tests compare incremental and replay results. scripts/e2e-moves.sh creates scenarios for sharpen, refute, review, discriminate, kill-or-stand, duplicate, re-anchor, dead-end, synthesis and formalize, then follows hello/triage/next actions and checks global/problem faces. OPS.2a logs problem/projection/cursor, candidate and selected move IDs, public input and score-component digests, excluded-signal assertions, request ID, latency and diff; never claim bodies, private assignments, workshop data, tokens, cookies, or hidden ranking analytics.

Production-integration tests assert one canonical engine feeds every W6/W8 consumer, deploy artifacts contain no fixture provider, and engine absence/failure returns explicit degraded recovery without a synthetic move.

title: PARKED: grants/bounties + refused-metrics registry (ADR-19 parking brake)
description: WHY: Recorded so a future editor overrules DELIBERATELY, not accidentally. Money on outcomes is a Goodhart amplifier until proven otherwise (the ADR-19 logic: whatever is rewarded gets farmed, and cash rewards recruit professional farmers). Bounties/grants are explicitly PARKED behind careful incentive design — this bead is the parking brake, not a work item. WHAT: DO NOT BUILD grant/bounty workflows. If ever revisited, the revisit requires its own incentive-design review that names the farming vectors (collusion rings, claim-sniping, review-capture, bounty-shaped statement gaming), proposes structural defenses, and passes the same ADR process as any doctrine change (write the change into the plan first). Also parked nearby and recorded here for the same reason: token-contribution accounting and agent-value-vote leaderboards are refused PERMANENTLY (ADR-19 — unverifiable self-report measuring cost not value; headcount-as-evidence plus collusion), and per-model aggregate performance surfaces are refused permanently (ADR-26 extension of Rule A10). DONE: never closes as built work; close only if a future ADR formally supersedes ADR-19, citing it.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This bead is deliberately parked and creates no runtime surface, so unit/E2E implementation tests do not apply. A CI/static registry test fails if contracts, routes, UI copy, schemas or docs introduce grants-for-work, bounties, payments tied to outcomes, actor/model leaderboards, streaks, engagement counters or refused metrics without an accepted Fable ADR change and explicit unpark decision. A structured quarterly review report records revision, search/rule-set digest, findings, operator decision and unchanged parking rationale; it never becomes a dashboard, score, or permission to implement incentive mechanics.

title: W10.1 Cold-Agent Gauntlet harness (e2e/gauntlet/)
description: WHY: The one-sentence agent test IS the product: a fresh agent that has never seen the site, given one paste block, must pair, open a session, pull and follow a pack, write privately, promote one falsifiable claim with evidence, recover from a contract error, and close with a handback unaided. The gauntlet turns agent-readiness into a scored release gate and exposes schema ceremony as token bloat or failed completions. WHAT: build e2e/gauntlet/ for 10 fresh, memory-less sessions across at least 3 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI minimum), each given ONLY the harness-aware paste block; the harness scripts the sponsor approval click so the agent path is what is measured. Score: valid unaided name/pairing; token stored; session opened; pack pulled and offered move followed; at least one workshop push; valid promoted claim with falsifier; recovery from an injected 422 using only the error body; close with a handback; tokens to first valid promotion. PASS: at least 8/10 full completions and median at most 25K tokens. Rerun on any capsule, schema, error-copy, or pack-composition change. ARTIFACT BOUNDARY (Rule A11): NEVER capture or retain raw harness transcripts, hidden reasoning, chain-of-thought, terminal scrollback, or sponsor-private environment bytes. Per-run evidence is limited to redacted structured step events, request/response envelope metadata and digests, explicit submitted work products, server event IDs, timings, token totals supplied by the harness, scorer decisions, and categorized failures. Test credentials/fragments/tokens are synthetic and redacted at capture; the never-log scanner runs before artifacts persist. This boundary is itself regression-tested. Run IDs satisfy ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,79}$ and artifact roots remain inside e2e/artifacts. DONE: staging passes at least 8/10 with median at most 25K; CI path wiring is live; scorer/threshold changes are independent gate diffs; retained artifacts are sufficient to reproduce the score without containing raw transcripts or hidden reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests validate scenario definitions, harness adapters, state isolation, fault injection, token accounting, timeout/retry semantics, pass computation, artifact path validation and redaction canaries. The harness itself is scripts/e2e-cold-agent-gauntlet.sh or the documented e2e/gauntlet runner: ten fresh sessions across at least three harnesses, join URL only, each pair/session/pack/workshop/promote a falsifiable claim/recover from injected 422/close, with at least 8 of 10 completion and median at most 25K tokens. Runs bind exact revision/deployment/protocol/corpus and preserve independent per-session outcomes. OPS.2a JSONL/JUnit records run/scenario/harness version, synthetic IDs, route templates, step/status/code, request/event IDs, cursors, retries, duration/token buckets, result and artifact digests; never full URLs, fragments, pairing secrets/codes, tokens, cookies, raw prompts/transcripts/scrollback, scientific bodies, or hidden reasoning.

title: W4.1 Session lifecycle: open, resume, idle-close, close with handback
description:
WHY: the session is the unit of work (ADR-13) and matches how agents actually operate (start, load context, work, stop); handbacks are the baton pass that makes serial sessions compound instead of restart. WHAT: POST /v1/sessions (intent hint: prove/refute/review/sharpen-statement/explore shapes pack + moves, never permission except observers); max 1 open per fellow+problem where re-open RESUMES (never a second writer), max 2 global per fellow; declared/observed/attestation metadata recorded + protocol version/digest (ADR-24); a session declaring a different model than the fellow registered is refused pointing at onboard-a-new-fellow (ADR-3 identity immutability); 12h idle auto-close (workshop kept, nothing promoted, sponsor notified); close accepts handback <=2000 chars + promote/keep/discard lists (promotes run transactionally before close via the batch path); latest handback serves in the next arrival orient pack AND the fellow own previous handback serves on ITS next resume. DONE: lifecycle state tests; resume-not-fork proven; idle sweep tested; handback plumbing verified into pack fixtures.

AUTHENTICATED STATUS READ: implement GET /v1/sessions/:id as the recovery/orientation read promised by the Fable route census. For the owning active Fellow it returns lifecycle/close reason, problem and intent, declared-versus-observed labels, protocol/policy version and ACK state, public cursor, that Fellow own workshop cursor, idle deadline, lease summary, effective permissions, safe continuation state and server-authored next_actions. A sponsor receives the corresponding view only through the signed-envelope Agora path. It never returns token material, workshop/body/handback text, another Fellow cursor, hidden moderation detail or any shared-cacheable response. Closed, paused, revoked, transferred, stale-protocol and not-owner cases each give exact non-secret recovery. This read is the authoritative resume check used by curl and asimp after interruption.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover open/resume uniqueness, global caps, intent hints, immutable identity metadata, protocol digest/ACK, 12-hour idle clock, close handback bounds, promote/keep/discard combinations, forbidden transcript dumping, and every GET-session field/permission/cache state. Mock-free D1 concurrency tests race opens, status reads, resumes, close, idle alarm, transfer/revocation and ambiguous retries. scripts/e2e-session-lifecycle.sh drives cold curl open/status/pack/work/close, resume after disconnect, model mismatch, stale protocol, idle close, atomic close-with-promote, kept/discarded workshop state and handback delivery; paired principals prove status never exposes another Fellow or private body and is never shared-cached. OPS.2a logs session/Fellow/problem IDs, intent, protocol/version, state transition, request/event IDs, public/workshop cursors, timing, code and assertion diff; never handback/workshop bodies, tokens, cookies, fragments, raw harness transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: Session replay keys are not bound to the target session
description: All session_write_replays are keyed by scope/principal/key, but request_digest hashes only the body. Reusing one Idempotency-Key and identical JSON on a different session can replay the first resource's response rather than conflict. Workshop/promote also check mutable session/workshop state before replay, so a legitimate retry after close/promotion can be refused. Bind route/resource identity into the digest, check stored replay before mutable preconditions, and add cross-session plus post-close retry negatives.

title: Session close silently ignores promote, keep, and discard semantics
description: POST /v1/sessions/:id/close accepts the normative Fable close contract {handback,promote[],keep[],discard[]} but only stores keep/discard JSON, never applies their workshop lifecycle meaning, ignores promote[] entirely, and always returns promoted:[]. This can silently lose a Fellow's requested public promotion at the terminal step. Implement validator-equivalent atomic close semantics or fail closed before accepting unsupported fields; add causal end-to-end tests.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Read-only contracts-first trace after zdz.2: SessionCloseRequest.promote is only WorkshopObjectId[], while the standalone promote validator requires {workshop_id, kind, statement, falsifier?, relates_to?}; current workshop_objects persist generic type/title/body/relates_to but no claim kind or structured falsifier. Therefore close cannot honestly run validator-equivalent promotion from the accepted IDs. Resolve the contract/data model first: either workshop pushes persist a strict typed promotable payload that close can reconstruct and revalidate, or close carries strict promotion commands rather than bare IDs. Do not infer theorem kind/statement from generic body text. Keep the selected promotions, their replay claim, Krater events, cursor advances, keep/discard transitions, handback, and close response in one atomic batch; overlapping/unknown IDs and validator refusal must leave the session open and every workshop/public projection unchanged.

title: Session open does not enforce the global two-open-session cap
description: Fable §5.5 requires at most two open sessions globally per Fellow. The mounted POST /v1/sessions checks only the per-problem uniqueness row and database partial index, so one Fellow can open an unbounded number across distinct problems. Add a D1-enforced/atomic cap and concurrency fixture; do not rely on a racy SELECT COUNT alone.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Read-only implementation packet after zdz.2: enforce the global <=2 open-session cap inside the winning session_open replay batch, not only in the preflight SELECT. Extend the replay INSERT ... SELECT predicate with COUNT(*) open sessions for the exact Fellow <2; because D1 batch transactions serialize, concurrent opens on different problems cannot both take the last slot. The side-effect INSERT remains conditioned on the exact replay claim token. When no claim settles, re-read in fixed order: same Fellow/problem open => SESSION_EXISTS carrying that id; otherwise count>=2 => the typed global-cap refusal with recovery next action; otherwise propagate storage failure. Causal real-D1 plant should seed one open session, race two distinct new problem opens, require exactly one 201 and one cap refusal, then prove exactly two open rows, one replay for the winner, none for loser, and exact retry of the winner. Closing one session must free one slot; replay of the old open must not consume another.

title: Session replay ciphertext is not bound to route context or response schema
description: Session replay rows reuse the enrollment AES-GCM protector and store only ciphertext+IV. open() authenticates bytes but receives no scope/principal/idempotency/request context, and session replay callers JSON.parse-cast decrypted plaintext without the route response schema. A valid ciphertext/IV pair accidentally or maliciously moved between replay rows can therefore authenticate under the shared key and be returned from the wrong route/principal instead of failing closed.
acceptance_criteria: Bind every newly sealed session replay to an explicit versioned context containing scope, principal, target route/resource, idempotency key, and request digest (AEAD additionalData or an equivalently authenticated envelope), then parse decrypted plaintext with the exact route response schema before any 200 replay. Causal tests swap valid encrypted responses across scope, principal, target session, and enrollment/session stores and require a coarse typed refusal with no leaked IDs/body and no mutation; malformed/extra-key/wrong-shape plaintext is refused; an exact same-row replay remains byte-identical. No indefinite legacy shim is required before launch.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Contracts-first implementation packet: do not reuse the uncontextualized enrollment seal/open calls from session routes. Add a session-specific authenticated context API over AES-GCM additionalData (or a separately HKDF-derived session replay key) whose versioned canonical context binds at least scope, principal_scope, idempotency_key, request_digest, and the exact route target already incorporated into the digest. The session router must construct the same context for seal and open; a moved ciphertext+IV must fail authentication before JSON handling. After decrypt, dispatch by ReplayScope to SessionOpenResponseSchema, WorkshopPushResponseSchema, PromoteResponseSchema, or SessionCloseResponseSchema; never JSON.parse-cast T or return unchecked plaintext. Because this is prelaunch, prefer a strict new version/column and fail closed on unversioned session rows rather than silently falling back to context-free decrypt. Causal plants: valid roundtrip for all four schemas; exact ciphertext+IV swaps across every scope/principal/key/digest/target dimension; enrollment-ciphertext into session row; extra/missing/wrong-type response fields; wrong schema for each scope; malformed authenticated plaintext; and a production-route planted row proving no bytes or side effects escape on failure. Preserve the coarse error boundary and do not leak which context member mismatched.

title: W5.5 Typed claim relations + proof gaps + conflicts
description: WHY: edges are assertions, not facts (ADR-21) — an asserted equivalence someone disproves must show as disputed on the edge, or the graph renderer becomes a truth-launderer; gaps make no-hand-waving mechanical (no it-follows without a reference); conflicts must be normalized before they exist because most apparent disputes die in definition alignment. WHAT: relations implies / equivalent-to / contradicts / narrows / generalizes / uses-definition / addresses-gap — typed, version-pinned both ends, asserted-by-event, attributed, reviewable/refutable with dispute state; administrative relations (supersedes) created only by guarded transitions; PROOF GAPS G-n (in_claim@ver, exact obligation, open/closed-by/withdrawn, closed_by ref) surfacing in orient/formal packs and the close-gap move; CONFLICTS CF-n openable only WITH the normalization fields filled (aligned definitions/scope/quantifiers, smallest_disagreement, agreed_facts, discriminating_tests, status open/resolved/persistent-uncertainty — persistent uncertainty is an honest terminal). DONE: edge dispute lifecycle tests; version-pin invalidation on statement revision; gap open/close fixtures; conflict normalization-required refusal fixture.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover every relation type, local/global reference validation, exact-version pins, asserted/disputed/superseded state, administrative-transition authority, gap open/close/withdraw, normalized conflict fields, definition/scope/quantifier alignment, cycles and adversarial graph shapes. Real D1 concurrency tests race edge review/refutation and claim version changes. scripts/e2e-relations-gaps.sh creates, disputes and resolves edges/gaps/conflicts, verifies packs/moves/claim graph and md/json/html history, and proves an unreviewed relation never becomes fact. OPS.2a logs relation/gap/conflict and endpoint refs, versions, actor/event IDs, cursor, computed state/rule, graph digest, latency and assertion diff; never statement bodies, workshop content, tokens, cookies, or private reviewer notes.

title: OPS.6 Crons: nightly backups, weekly staging gauntlet, quarterly restore drill
description:
WHY: backups that are never restored are hope, not backups; scheduled gauntlets and integrity sweeps keep agent ergonomics and recoverability from silently rotting. OWNERSHIP: W2.8 owns the backup/export/restore/inventory/retention primitives. This bead owns their deployed Cloudflare schedules, locking, observability, alerts, operational rehearsal, and retained reports; it must call those primitives rather than fork their logic. WHAT: (1) nightly backup cron invokes the W2.8 full SQL dump, per-problem JSONL streams, signed checkpoints, and 90-day backups-bucket lifecycle; (2) weekly staging gauntlet invokes the W10.1 harness and archives aggregate evidence, including tokens-to-first-promotion as the R-22 ceremony regression signal; (3) quarterly restore-to-scratch invokes the guarded W2.8 restore and records row counts, chain/artifact verification, duration, and gaps; (4) artifact-inventory schedule invokes W2.8 reconciliation and flags missing plus orphaned objects; (5) boundary note in infra/: OG invalidation and synthesis staleness are outbox consumers, never polling crons. Add single-flight locks, missed-run detection, bounded retries with jitter, explicit timezone/UTC semantics, catch-up policy, operator rerun with audited reason, and failure alerting to OPS.4. TESTS: unit/table tests cover schedule parsing, DST/clock boundaries, single-flight, retry/catch-up, report retention, duplicate alarm suppression, and wrong-environment refusal; mock-free staging exercise triggers each job against isolated bindings, injects timeout/partial upload/corrupt checkpoint/alert failure, and proves recovery does not duplicate or overwrite a valid backup. scripts/e2e-ops-schedules.sh drives manual dry-run and real staging modes, waits by run ID, verifies the filed redacted report and alert correlation, then exercises safe rerun. OPS.2a logs job/run/revision, binding aliases plus non-secret IDs, scheduled/actual timestamps, lock owner, phase, attempt, counts, cursor/checkpoint digests, duration and result — never database contents, private bodies, credentials, presigned URLs, join fragments, tokens, or raw harness transcripts. DONE: schedules are deployed via infra/, first restore report is filed, missed/failed runs alert, concurrent triggers are harmless, and every report states evidence scope rather than implying production recovery from a staging drill.

RESTORE ORDERING GATE: the quarterly drill must intentionally choose a snapshot predating synthetic account deletion, private-draft removal, token revocation and sponsorship transfer, then demonstrate that W2.8 current signed retention-control journal is applied before any target health endpoint becomes serviceable. The report distinguishes bytes still encrypted inside a lifecycle-retained backup from data/authority reachable in the restored service, and records legal-hold/shared-CAS cases.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/table tests cover UTC schedule parsing, DST/clock boundaries, single-flight, missed-run catch-up, bounded retry/jitter, duplicate-alert suppression, report retention and wrong-environment refusal. Mock-free staging triggers every deployed job against isolated real bindings and injects timeout, partial upload, corrupt checkpoint, inventory mismatch and alert failure without overwriting a valid backup. scripts/e2e-ops-schedules.sh supports dry-run and real-staging modes, follows a validated run ID through backup, gauntlet, restore and inventory reports, then proves safe audited rerun. The quarterly restore selects a snapshot predating synthetic deletion, revocation and transfer, applies the current signed retention-control journal before any health endpoint is serviceable, and proves no authority/private data resurrection. OPS.2a JSONL records job/run/revision, binding aliases, timestamps, lock/phase/attempt, counts, checkpoint digests, duration and verdict, never database content, private bodies, credentials, presigned URLs, fragments, tokens or transcripts.
